stories.primary_headline: Oil companies challenge Karnataka's claim of excess ethanol in petrol, question testing methodology

primary_source.headline: Oil companies challenge Karnataka's claim of excess ethanol in petrol, question testing methodology
primary_source.content: New Delhi: State-run oil marketing companies Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL), and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) have challenged Karnataka government's claims that petrol sold at certain outlets in the state contained 26-31 per cent ethanol, questioning the sampling and testing procedures used to arrive at the findings.The three companies said E20 petrol supplied across their retail networks, including Karnataka, conforms to the Bureau of Indian Standards' IS 17021 specifications, which prescribe an ethanol content of 19-21 per cent.In a joint statement, the oil companies said the findings cited by the Karnataka government were not supported by tests conducted in accordance with the prescribed statutory and technical procedures. They also questioned the use of third-party laboratory certificates that, they said, did not disclose sufficient details of the testing methodology to independently verify the reported ethanol levels.The dispute centres on a testing exercise conducted in October 2026 by Karnataka's Department of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology, which claimed that petrol samples collected from certain retail outlets contained substantially higher ethanol concentrations than the prescribed limit.The OMCs said the sampling procedure mandated under the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005, read with the Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) 2024, requires six one-litre samples to be collected.Of these, two samples must be handed over to the dealer against acknowledgement, two retained by the oil company or department, and two sent to a laboratory specified under the control order. Sample labels must be jointly signed, with test results communicated to the dealer and oil company within the prescribed timeframe.While samples collected during a September exercise were routed through the State Level Coordinator to designated OMC laboratories, the companies said the subsequent October sampling was conducted without their representatives.They said they had not received the corresponding retention samples, outlet-wise details or laboratory reports despite seeking them through the state-level coordinator, denying them and the dealers an opportunity to independently verify the findings or seek retesting.The companies also questioned the testing methodology cited in the laboratory certificates. Under IS 17021:2018, as amended in August 2025, ethanol content in E20 petrol must be determined through specified methods, including Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy, water extraction or gas chromatography under prescribed ASTM standards.Where gas chromatography is used, the standard requires the sample to be diluted in a 1:1 ratio with oxygenate-free petrol and the result corrected against an E10 certified reference material.The Karnataka certificates, however, merely mentioned ethanol percentage determined through gas chromatography without specifying the applicable test standard, dilution procedure or reference material used, the OMCs said.They argued that the reported ethanol levels of 26-31 per cent could not be independently validated without these details.The companies also flagged discrepancies in the density readings. The certificates reportedly showed densities of 0.742-0.749 grams per cubic centimetre for samples claimed to contain 26-31 per cent ethanol, against 0.752-0.760 grams per cubic centimetre recorded in E20 samples tested by the OMCs.Since ethanol has a higher density than petrol, a higher ethanol concentration would ordinarily be expected to increase the density of the blend, they said, adding that the discrepancy warranted verification using prescribed testing methods and reference samples.Seeking to counter the Karnataka findings, the companies cited a nationwide quality-monitoring exercise conducted by the OMCs and the Centre for High Technology (CHT), under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.Up to 31.2% ethanol in petrol: Karnataka govt alleges oil companies sell blends exceeding prescribed limitsUnder the OMC/CHT Quality Coordination Cell exercise, 893 E20 samples collected from depots and retail outlets of the three companies across 27 states and Union Territories were tested at refinery and OMC quality-control laboratories.All 893 samples were found to contain ethanol within the prescribed 19-21 per cent range, according to the companies.The results included 56 samples from Karnataka, drawn from different locations and covering all three OMCs. These recorded ethanol content of 19-20 per cent, averaging 19.30 per cent, they said.The companies said ethanol blending at refineries and depots was carried out through calibrated and automated proportioning systems, with quality-control protocols governing the process. Blending was not a manual or arbitrary exercise, they added.The companies also questioned estimates cited in the Karnataka controversy that E20 fuel could result in annual consumer mileage losses of around Rs 62,000 crore and vehicle repair expenses of Rs 39,000 crore, taking the combined impact to approximately Rs 1.01 lakh crore.They said such estimates required scientific substantiation and could not be based on a blanket assumption of 10 per cent mileage loss across the country's vehicle population.More than 30 crore two-wheelers and 4 crore four-wheelers have been running on E20 fuel for over three years, while more than 6 crore people visit petrol pumps daily, the companies said.They argued that the absence of any reported widespread vehicle breakdowns was an important consideration in assessing concerns over fuel quality and vehicle performance.Citing the Petroleum Ministry's August 12, 2025 response on ethanol blending, the OMCs said studies involving the Inter-Ministerial Committee, Indian Oil, the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) had examined the performance implications of E20.Vehicles calibrated for E20 could experience mileage reductions of around 1-2 per cent, while certain other vehicles could see declines of 3-6 per cent, depending on vehicle category and calibration, according to the ministry's assessment.The companies said the Rs 39,000 crore estimate for vehicle repairs also needed to be supported by actual vehicle-performance data, materials compatibility studies and documented repair costs.India's ethanol-blending programme, which began with a pilot initiative in 2001, is aimed at reducing dependence on imported crude oil, strengthening domestic agricultural value chains and improving energy security.The programme has been expanded through successive policy interventions, including the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018, and the NITI Aayog roadmap for ethanol blending.According to Petroleum Ministry data cited by the OMCs, the programme since the 2014-15 ethanol supply year has generated foreign exchange savings of more than Rs 1.97 lakh crore, substituted approximately 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil, reduced carbon dioxide emissions by around 952 lakh metric tonnes and resulted in payments of more than Rs 1.66 lakh crore to farmers.During the 2025-26 ethanol supply year, which ended on October 31, 2026, the three public sector OMCs procured 1,089 crore litres of ethanol and blended 1,134 crore litres against petrol sales of approximately 5,673 crore litres, the statement said.The companies also rejected suggestions that they had a commercial incentive to blend ethanol beyond prescribed levels, arguing that additional ethanol procurement would increase their costs.The three OMCs have asked the Karnataka government to share complete sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports and details of the testing methodology used to arrive at the reported findings.They have also sought access to the counterpart samples for independent testing at an authorised laboratory using the prescribed referee method, in the presence of representatives of both the state government and the oil companies.The companies said they were willing to participate in joint sampling and testing in accordance with the Control Order and MDG 2024, adding that any deviation established through the prescribed procedure would be dealt with under applicable guidelines.

brief_bullets: Jay Rockefeller, the prominent Democratic politician and heir to the legendary Rockefeller dynasty, has passed away at age 89. Serving as West Virginia’s governor and a U.S. senator for three decades, he distinguished himself by championing healthcare reform and securing insurance for millions of low-income children through the Children’s Health Insurance Program. Despite his family’s deep-rooted Republican ties, Rockefeller forged a unique political identity centered on public service and social advocacy within the Appalachian region. His death marks the end of a significant era in American politics, reflecting a legacy defined by his transition from a wealthy industrialist lineage to a dedicated public servant who fundamentally reshaped federal healthcare policy for the nation’s most vulnerable populations.
why_it_matters_bullets: His legacy underscores the enduring impact of bipartisan legislative efforts on expanding social safety nets for American families.

primary_source.content: New Delhi: After a delay, the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) finally announced the dates for class 10 and 12 examinations. Exams for both the classes will begin on February 16, with physics being the first paper for Class 12 and painting the first for Class 10. The exams will conclude on March 9 for Class 10 and April 9 for Class 12.The exams, which will be held offline in pen-paper model, will be conducted across 86 subjects for Class 10, and for Class 12, students will appear across 121 subjects.CBSE Board Exams 2027: Practical exams from January 1; Class 10, 12 date sheet awaited“Adequate gaps have been provided between examinations of subjects commonly offered together by students in both Class X and Class XII. The tentative schedules of major entrance examinations for Class XII students have been taken  into account. Every effort has been made to complete the Board Examinations well before the commencement of such entrance examinations, enabling students to manage their preparation effectively,” CBSE said in a release. The board also said that it has further taken into account the number of candidates appearing on a particular day at each examination centre to facilitate smooth conduct of examinations. They added that the schedule was designed to minimise the prolonged absence of teachers from their schools during the evaluation process.In all, the Board said, it factored in 40,000 subject combinations while designing the exam sheet.

stories.primary_headline: "Not applied its mind..." Gauhati High Court quashes Pranab Doley's detention order under NSA

primary_source.headline: "Not applied its mind..." Gauhati High Court quashes Pranab Doley's detention order under NSA
primary_source.content: Guwahati: More than 100 days after Pranab Doley, an indigenous rights activist in Assam, was detained under the National Security Act (NSA), Gauhati High Court on Friday quashed the order of his detention on the ground that the same was legally unsustainable.While quashing the detention order, the court observed that the detaining authority did not apply its mind as to whether or not the ordinary laws of the country was insufficient to deal with the activities of the petitioner.The bench of justice Kalyan Rai Surana and Justice Susmita Phukan Khaund had reserved its judgment on October 14. The 34-page judgment was pronounced on Friday.'He just raised voice for people, did nothing anti-national': Father of NSA detenue Pranab Doley Doley, who allegedly led indigenous farmers near Kaziranga National Park for a protest against construction of a five-star hotel allegeldly without properly compensating them, was arrested on July 13. He was, however, granted bail on July 29 but was detained under the NSA a day later. In the detention order, the state home department claimed that Doley was booked in several criminal cases in the past and his prevention detention was necessary in view of possibility of him continue to indulge in "activities prejudicial to maintenance of law and order." The court set aside the detention order on the grounds that Doley, 40, was detained on the strength of "stale cases," including those in which he had been discharged and acquitted. The court said out of the 13 cases, Doley had been acquitted in nine while legal process was underway in the rest. The bench said although the detaining authority alleged Doley's involvement in road blockades and damages to public properties, no particulars of the alleged offence, including place, dateand time of commission of such alleged offences have been disclosed. "Thus, the allegations against the petitioner is vague and bereft of material particulars..."The court said relevant facts and grounds of his detention and relevant documents were not furnished to Doley, disallowing him to make an effective representation before the prescribed authorities. The authorities also did not act on his representation against his detention, the court said. Foreign trips: The HC said although the home department claimed that Doley had visited foreign countries 14 times, it did not give the details of anti-India activity by the petitioner. "The grounds of detention also does not specify in which foreign visit the petitioner made any speech or statement which has brought disrepute to the country or has encouraged seditious activity against the country. There is no information as to where the petitioner gave any speech or statement, which had the potential to threaten the security or integrity of the country, territorial, moral, political, social, or otherwise."The bench said Doley's repetitive foreign visits, by itself, is not an act which would warrant preventive detention of a person and curtail his fundamental right to visit a country of his choice. "....except for a vagu allegation regarding foreign visits and suspicious foreign exchange receipts, the detaining authority has not furnished to the petitioner any materials showing how his foreign visits and receipt of foreign exchange amounts to activities that is prejudicial to the interest of the State, its security and integrity, or has affected public order," the court said.Three lawyers, Santanu Borthakur, Dipesh Kumar Agarwala and S. Dey appeared on behalf of Doley. Timeline of eventsDoley, who did Master in Social Work from TISS, Mumbai, was arrested on July 13 following a protest against construciton of a 5-star hotel near Kaziranga National Park without allegedly compensating the indigenous farmers.He was granted bail on July 29.He was detained under the NSA on July 30.State home department claimed that Doley's prevention detention was necessary in view of possibility of him continue to indulge in "activities prejudicial to maintenance of law and order." His father Lakhi Doley had said Pranab was detained for raising voice for the indigenous farmers.

stories.primary_headline: 'Step into the Light': Juhi Chawla makes surprise cameo in latest 'Shot on iPhone 18 Pro' ad ahead of Diwali

primary_source.headline: 'Step into the Light': Juhi Chawla makes surprise cameo in latest 'Shot on iPhone 18 Pro' ad ahead of Diwali
primary_source.content: For years, Apple has been a master at marketing its products, especially with the Shot on iPhone feature ads. It has good knack of finding the art directors who are capable of capturing the local cultural aspects and also flawlessly highlight the photography capabilities of the new iPhones.With soaring demand for iPhone 18 Pro models worldwide, Apple has released fun, catchy ad- 'Step into the Light' with popular music track-- Roop Suhana Lagta Hai- composed by Anu Malik in the 1994 film 'The Gentleman', starring legendary Telugu star Chiranjeevi and Bollywood icon Juhi Chawla ahead of Diwali (aka Deepavali).Apple Watch saves senior doctor: Timely alert helps him get heart valve surgery done in the nick of timeDirected by Sanjay Garg (Raw Mango founder), the new 'Shot on iPhone' ad features ptures how India looks during the festival of light. The video was filmed at Tijara Fort, a restored 19th-century royal palace in Rajasthan.The film’s concept revolves around stepping out of darkness into light through dance. Also, it brings together a diverse cast from across India, each wearing Raw Mango looks with details specific to their region.The icing on the cake is the surprise cameo by the OG Juhi Chawla, the lead female protagonist from the movie 'The Gentleman'.Juhi Chawla on Shot on iPhone 18 Pro ad.“Diwali, for me, is the biggest festival of the year. It represents a change in weather where we welcome winter in the company of people we love,” said Sanjay Garg.Behind-the-scene: Apple's shot on iPhone 18 Pro ad (screen-grab)With light at the centre of the Diwali festival, the film, as you can see in the video (below), was shot in low light to showcase the most advanced cameras of the iPhone 18 Pro series.The biggest upgrade we see in the iPhone 18 Pro is the dynamic variable aperture. Apple achieved this feat by incorporating six laser-cut blades, which can smoothly transition between different apertures, making it incredibly simple to capture the best shot by automatically adjusting for depth of field and lighting.Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max Review: Powerful performer with exceptionally good cameraCombined with a new sensor that improves image quality, the result is better low-light photography, crisper detail in the back of group photos, and more unique shots.Also, the variable aperture offers more control for creative filmmakers to manually adjust any of the four aperture settings in the native camera app.Tips & Tricks: Master Deepavali photography on the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone DuoGet the latest news on new launches, gadget reviews, apps, cybersecurity, and more on personal technology only on DH Tech.

stories.primary_headline: TCS Nashik case: AIMIM leader Imtiyaz Jaleel named as accused in supplementary chargesheet

primary_source.headline: TCS Nashik case: AIMIM leader Imtiyaz Jaleel named as accused in supplementary chargesheet
primary_source.content: Nashik: All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) leader Imtiyaz Jaleel has been named an accused by police in a supplementary chargesheet, filed in the sexual harassment and religious conversion case at TCS's Nashik unit, for allegedly helping a key accused when she was absconding.The supplementary chargesheet was filed in the court of Additional Sessions Judge Amit Kharkar in Nashik on Friday, a lawyer representing one of the victims said.Jaleel, a former Lok Sabha MP from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (formerly Aurangabad), is accused of helping Nida Khan, a former employee at the TCS Nashik unit and a key accused in the case, when she was absconding.The Nashik police Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case at Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) Nashik unit had found connection of Jaleel with AIMIM corporator Mateen Patel, who had been arrested earlier for giving shelter to Nida during her stay in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.Accordingly, a notice under section 35 (3) of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was served to Jaleel around a month ago, seeking his appearance. The AIMIM Maharashtra unit president subsequently appeared for questioning before the SIT.Now, the SIT has named Jaleel an accused in the chargesheet related to the case registered at the Deolali Camp police station, said the lawyer.Jaleel did not appear in the court and further proceedings will take place as per legal procedures. The court will issue a summons and Jaleel will have to appear before it or apply for bail.TCS sexual harassment case: Five accused given bail by Nashik courtAs per the SIT, Nida was harboured by Patel, the AIMIM corporator from Naregao in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, around 200km away from Nashik, in central Maharashtra when police were searching for her. Patel was questioned and arrested on August 8.A case was registered against Patel as well as co-accused Hanif Khan, owner of the flat where Nida was living.The first TCS case was registered at the Deolali Camp police station on March 26. On May 2, a local court rejected her bail application. Khan was arrested from Naregao on May 7 and the court granted her bail on July 6.The SIT is probing a total of nine cases registered in connection with the alleged exploitation, attempt of forceful conversion, hurting religious sentiments, molestation and mental harassment of female employees at the TCS unit.Eight cases were filed at the Mumbai Naka police station in Nashik and one at the Deolali Camp police station. Eight victims came forward with their complaints, and according to police, these incidents were taking place at the unit since July 2022.Nida's specific role, according to the investigation, involved brainwashing one of the victims by giving her a burqa and religious literature.The SIT had earlier filed two chargesheets in the case, in which nearly a dozen people have been named accused so far.After the case came to light, TCS maintained it has adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards harassment and coercion of any form at workplace for a long time.

He was addressing gathering after inaugurating a public meeting organised as part of Bharatiya Janata Party’s ‘Save Democracy, End Anarchy campaign at Kadri ground. Suresh Gopi quoting a verse from renowned Tamil poet Subramania Bharathiyar's famous poem, ‘Bharata Samudayam Vazhgave; Vazhga Vazhga Bharata Samudayam Vazhgave’, declared that it was unfortunate that a ruling party had been compelled to organise a protest in response to an agitation organised by the opposition.He alleged that those spreading misinformation about the SIR, which is being undertaken to ensure the integrity of electoral politics, were misleading the country’s youth. Mangaluru: Union minister Suresh Gopi to take part in march against Congress over electoral rolls misinformation“Kharge’s son should understand that Narendra Modi is not going anywhere from this country. It is your leader and his family who should leave. If they do not go voluntarily, the people themselves will lift them up and throw them into the Arabian Sea,” Suresh Gopi declared.He added that the protest meeting was only the beginning and warned that the anger of the people would engulf all those opposing the initiative.BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia, BJP DK district president Satish Kumpala, Udupi district president Naveen Shetty Kuthyaru, Kasaragod district president N L Ashwini, MP Captain Brijesh Chowta, Kota Srinivas Poojary, MLAs D Vedavyas Kamath, Harish Poonja, Rajesh Naik Ulipadyguthu, K Umanath Kotian, Gurme Suresh Shetty, Bhagirathi Murulya, Gururaj Gantihole, Dr Y Bharath Shetty, Yashpal Suvarna, Kiran Kumar Kodgi, MLCs Kishore Kumar Puttur, Pratapsimha Nayak among olthers participated in the meeting.

stories.primary_headline: IMA urges CBFC to deny certification to Sunny Deol-starrer, says film glorifies violence against medics

primary_source.headline: IMA urges CBFC to deny certification to Sunny Deol-starrer, says film glorifies violence against medics
primary_source.content:
New Delhi: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has urged the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) to refuse certification to the upcoming Hindi film Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak, alleging that its teaser glorifies violence against doctors.In a representation to the CBFC chairperson dated November 4, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak said the film, starring Sunny Deol and Ravi Kishan, attributes corruption to doctors as a class and presents assaulting doctors and hospital personnel inside a hospital as a "justified and heroic act."Directed by M Padmakumar, the film is scheduled for a nationwide theatrical release on November 20. Its official teaser was released on YouTube on October 19.The IMA said the teaser contains dialogues alleging that doctors charge exorbitant amounts, conduct unnecessary tests and accept commissions instead of writing prescriptions."Doctors don't write prescriptions; they write their commissions," the lead character says in the teaser, according to the representation.It also objects to scenes showing the lead character physically assaulting doctors, nursing staff and hospital personnel inside a hospital, claiming that such acts are presented as heroic and justified."The Film is likely to incite the commission of offences against doctors and other healthcare professionals, is against the interests of public order, involves defamation of registered medical practitioners as a body, and glorifies and justifies violence against doctors," the representation said.The association cited incidents of attacks on healthcare professionals across the country, including the stabbing death of a 22-year-old intern, Dr Vandana Das, in Kerala in May 2023, the assault on a doctor at a hospital in Kozhikode in October 2025 and attacks on resident doctors in Aligarh and Mumbai this year.'Satluj' director Honey Trehan criticises new CBFC guidelines, calls them 'cowardness and dictatorship'
It also cited a survey of 1,566 healthcare workers by experts from VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital and AIIMS, reported in May 2026, which found that 58.2 per cent of them felt unsafe at their workplace and 78.4 per cent had faced threats while on duty.The IMA said assaults on doctors by patients, relatives and attendants are a recurring feature of Indian hospitals and that the potential of the film to incite violence must be assessed in the prevailing conditions.It argued that violence in hospitals affects the community at large as attacks can disrupt medical services, endanger patients awaiting treatment and create an atmosphere of fear among healthcare workers.The association said the film violates Section 5B of the Cinematograph Act, 1952, which prohibits certification of films that are against public order, involve defamation, or are likely to incite the commission of an offence.It also cited the revised Guidelines for Certification of Films for Public Exhibition issued on September 16, arguing that the film violates provisions prohibiting glorification or justification of violence, depiction of visuals likely to incite offences and content involving defamation of an individual or a body of individuals.The IMA said the film's "objectionable" content forms its core theme and cannot be removed through mere excisions.It requested the CBFC to exhibit the film before IMA representatives and allow a medical expert nominated by the association to view it along with the examining committee.The association also sought an opportunity to be heard before any certification decision is taken and urged the board to refer the film to a revising committee if the examining committee recommends certification.The IMA said the film had not been submitted to the CBFC for certification as of October 22, according to the Information and Broadcasting Ministry.

brief_bullets: The Indian Medical Association has petitioned the Central Board of Film Certification to withhold clearance from the upcoming Hindi film Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak, starring Sunny Deol, arguing its teaser normalizes and glorifies violence against healthcare workers. Led by national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak, the medical body asserts that the M Padmakumar-directed project defames practitioners as corrupt and depicts hospital assaults as heroic acts, violating Section 5B of the Cinematograph Act. Citing a pervasive climate of fear and recent high-profile attacks on medical professionals nationwide, the IMA warns that the theatrical release risks inciting real-world hostility and severely disrupting public order.
why_it_matters_bullets: The controversy highlights mounting tensions over media depictions of professional corruption and the precarious safety conditions of healthcare workers.

OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?

brief_bullets: OpenAI has launched GPT-6 Cyber, a frontier artificial intelligence model carrying a critical cybersecurity rating, designed to assist defenders in preemptively securing digital infrastructure. Utilizing an earlier iteration through OpenAI's Daybreak Blue program, independent researcher Justicz successfully uncovered a complex, deeply buried vulnerability in the Debian Project's codebase within two hours, which has since been patched. why_it_matters_bullets: The rapid proliferation of AI-driven hacking tools severely threatens global digital infrastructure before defenders can adequately scale defenses.

sources.headline: India Set to Join EU's 93.5 Billion Euro Horizon Europe Research Program
India, EU conclude multi-billion Euro global innovation programme

brief_bullets: India and the European Union have successfully concluded negotiations for New Delhi to join the 93.5 billion euro Horizon Europe research and innovation program, effective January 2027. Led by the European Commission and Indian authorities, this agreement enables Indian universities, enterprises, and scientists to access direct funding and co-lead collaborative projects under Pillar II alongside European counterparts. stories.primary_headline: Karnataka High Court quashes POCSO charges against father, family members

primary_source.headline: Karnataka High Court quashes POCSO charges against father, family members
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: The Karnataka High Court has quashed proceedings against a man, his parents and sister under the provisions of the POCSO Act over allegations of sexual harassment on his minor child. “The innocence of childhood cannot be made the currency with which matrimonial scores are settled. Equally, the protection of a child cannot be sacrificed at the altar of a parent's claim of false implication,” Justice M Nagaprasanna said while allowing the petition filed by the father of the child and his family members.The estranged couple, residing in Bengaluru, had been involved in pleas over the custody and companionship of their minor daughter. The husband was awarded visitation rights as per the orders of the family court as well as the high court. Mangaluru court sentences two men to 20 years rigorous imprisonment in separate POCSO casesOn May 16 and May 17, 2026, the child was with the father but after returning, the mother alleged that the daughter complained of discomfort around her private parts. An FIR was registered under sections 8 and 10 of the POCSO Act against the father and other members of his family. Pursuant to the complaint, the mother approached the high court seeking cancellation/modification of the visitation rights granted to the father, citing the registration of the FIR. Challenging the FIR, the petitioners contended the allegation was made of sexual harassment of the minor child by the father and his family members.After perusing the affidavits placed by the doctors of the hospital where the child was subjected to medical examination, Justice Nagaprasanna noted that the complaints of discomfort were described as non-specific clinical findings. “Had the doctors expressed an opinion that the findings were attributable to sexual assault, the matter would have presented an altogether different complexion. That is not what the affidavits placed before this Court disclose,” the court said.The court further said that a contest for the custody and companionship of a minor daughter has resulted in drawing the child into the vortex of criminal litigation. “The child, who ought to have been the beneficiary of the affection of both parents, is now at the centre of their adversarial battle. The discord between the parents appears to have travelled far beyond the boundaries of their matrimonial relationship and threatens to cast its shadow upon the innocence, emotional security and well-being of the child,” Justice Nagaprasanna said.The court further said, “The criminal law cannot be reduced to a means of achieving indirectly what a litigant seeks to secure directly in proceedings concerning custody and visitation. The process of law is meant to advance justice, not to become the punishment itself.”

brief_bullets: The Karnataka High Court has quashed POCSO charges against a father and his family members, ruling that the allegations were weaponized during a contentious child custody battle. Justice M. Nagaprasanna determined that medical evidence failed to substantiate claims of sexual assault, describing the findings as non-specific and noting the absence of clinical proof. The court emphasized that the child was unfairly drawn into an adversarial parental dispute, warning that criminal litigation should not be used to settle matrimonial scores or manipulate visitation rights. By dismissing the FIR, the judiciary underscored that the integrity of child protection laws must be preserved against misuse, ensuring that legal processes serve justice rather than becoming tools for personal retaliation in domestic conflicts.

primary_source.headline: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw urges social media platforms to take greater responsibility for online harms
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Social media platforms must assume greater responsibility for the content they host, take necessary steps to ensure child safety, ensure algorithmic transparency, and provide citizens with an effective mechanism to address grievances, Union IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Friday.Speaking on the evolving nature of the internet and social media landscape, Vaishnaw asserted that platforms can no longer remain passive. They must proactively protect society from serious online harms, including “digital arrest” scams, he said. Kolkata teen blindfolded, set ablaze; police arrest 3, assault allegedly filmed for social media reel “Today, social media platforms must take the responsibility for child safety, for women’s safety, for digital arrest, for the harms which come to the citizens… social media platforms must take proactive steps. Unlike the past, they must take proactive steps to make sure that our society is safe,” said Vaishnaw, who also holds the Information and Broadcasting portfolio.The minister stressed the need to give ordinary citizens a stronger voice on these platforms. Currently, he noted, when content causes serious harm, the only options available are approaching the courts or the police. He called for a robust and effective grievance redressal system that allows people to seek remedies directly.“If something is there on the social media platforms which causes serious harm to the citizens, the citizens have only the recourse to go to the courts or go to the police. There has to be a good, very effective mechanism by which the citizens get voice to address their grievances,” Vaishnaw said.

stories.primary_headline: Minister raises concern over rising number of maternal deaths

primary_source.headline: Minister raises concern over rising number of maternal deaths
primary_source.content: Chitradurga: The rising number of maternal deaths despite the availability of modern facilities in hospitals is a matter of concern as maternal and infant mortality can be reduced if medical officers closely monitor the health of pregnant women, Health and Minority Welfare Minister U T Khader said.He was speaking at a progress review meeting of the health and minority welfare departments held at the deputy commissioner's office auditorium on Friday.Kannada vocabulary, dialects, folk knowledge and literary heritage must be preserved: Minister UT KhaderEven if pregnant women show minor signs of complications, they should immediately be shifted to the district hospital by ambulance. They should be admitted to hospitals at least three days before delivery. Doctors should ensure the health of both mother and child during childbirth. If serious complications arise, they should be referred to the district hospital. Awareness programmes must also be conducted in rural areas, he said.Four maternal deaths have been reported in the current year. The women died due to high blood pressure and lung infections. Compared to last year, the maternal mortality rate in the district has declined by 50%, District Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) Officer D M Abhinav said.Khata campaign sees 11,000 visitors in four weeks'Visit PHCs'The minister directed taluk health officers to visit and inspect primary health centres under their jurisdiction at least three times a month.During every visit, officers should identify deficiencies and problems and take steps to address them and introduce necessary improvements, he said.Meetings involving local MLAs, organisations and hospital staff should be held at least once a month. Hospitals should not have to wait for government funds for renovation, cleaning of toilets or painting. It is the responsibility of taluk health officers to seek assistance from local MLAs and organisations to renovate and maintain hospitals, he said.Minority schoolsResidential schools and colleges under the Minority Welfare Department should give importance to sports and extracurricular activities alongside quality education. It was encouraging that SSLC results in the district's APJ Abdul Kalam, Morarji Desai and Maulana Azad residential schools had exceeded 90%, he said.MLA K C Veerendra, Urban Development Authority chairperson M K Tajpeer, Deputy Commissioner S Ramya, Assistant Commissioner K Kantaraj, Health Department district nodal officer Ranganath, District Health Officer M C Sunil Kumar, District Guarantee Schemes Implementation Authority chairperson R Shivanna, and vice-chairperson D N Mailarappa, were present.Process e-khata applications in two days, open 10 PSK-style centres in Bengaluru: D K ShivakumarOutside prescriptionsIn another progress review meeting held at the Hiriyur City Municipal Council hall on Friday, Health Minister U T Khader warned government hospital doctors of strict action if they prescribe medicines that patients are required to purchase from outside."The government is supplying all necessary medicines to patients. Asking them to buy medicines from outside amounts to exploiting the poor. This should not continue," he warned.

sources.headline: Minister raises concern over rising number of maternal deaths

brief_bullets: Karnataka Health Minister U.T. Khader has expressed urgent concern over persistent maternal mortality rates in Chitradurga, despite the availability of modern medical infrastructure. During a departmental review, the Minister mandated that medical officers proactively monitor high-risk pregnancies, facilitate early hospital admissions, and ensure timely referrals to district facilities to mitigate complications like hypertension and infections. While local officials reported a 50 percent decline in maternal deaths compared to the previous year, Khader emphasized that further progress requires rigorous oversight of primary health centers and increased community awareness. He further warned government doctors against prescribing external medications, signaling a broader push for improved accountability and administrative efficiency within the state's public healthcare delivery system.
why_it_matters_bullets: Improving maternal health outcomes is critical for public trust and reflects the state's capacity to manage essential services.

stories.primary_headline: Looming water crisis: Lad asks officials to take preventive steps

primary_source.headline: Looming water crisis: Lad asks officials to take preventive steps
primary_source.content: Dharwad: District In-charge Minister Santosh Lad has urged people to use water judiciously and avoid wastage, warning that the severity of drought in the coming days cannot be predicted.Speaking at the KDP progress review meeting held at the Zilla Panchayat auditorium here on Friday, Lad said the possibility of a major water crisis in the coming days could not be ruled out and stressed the need for advance preparations by the government and public cooperation.He said discussions had already been held with officials of various departments on precautionary measures. The administration had identified vulnerable areas and taken decisions to tackle possible water shortages. Officials were directed to effectively implement schemes aimed at addressing drinking water problems.Lad warned that criminal cases would be registered against officials found negligent in implementing or maintaining water supply projects. Senior officers should monitor the performance of their subordinates daily and assign specific responsibilities to each official. Those failing to discharge their duties would face suspension, he said.MLA Abbayya Prasad expressed concern over the growing garbage menace in the twin cities. He urged the municipal corporation to prioritise waste management and ensure regular garbage clearance.He said civic officials should not restrict themselves to office work but conduct field inspections. Despite the appointment of zonal officers and provision of vehicles, the expected results had not been achieved. He suggested installing CCTV cameras at garbage dumping points and imposing fines on those violating waste disposal rules. Senior officials should also monitor the functioning of health inspectors and take action against those neglecting their duties.MLA N H Konaraddi stressed the need for officials to bring public and departmental issues to the notice of the concerned authorities without delay or concealing problems. Regular field visits and inspections were essential to understand and resolve public grievances, he said.Drought deepens drinking water crisis in Haveri districtMLA Vinay Kulkarni asked officials to respond responsibly to farmers’ and public grievances. Expressing concern over alleged corruption in government offices, he warned officials to curb the practice. Citing fodder shortage in the district, he directed that fodder should not be sold outside the district or state and that fodder supplied by the district administration should meet quality standards.He also directed the Superintendent of Police to investigate allegations that certain RTI activists were extorting money from government officials in the district.MLC F H Jakkappanavar called upon officials to ensure that SC and ST communities received their rightful reservation benefits and government grants. He also directed the authorities to clear encroachments on lakes and ensure that government circulars and decisions taken at meetings were implemented rather than remaining confined to files.MLAs M R Patil, MLC Lingaraj Patil, Deputy Commissioner Snehal R, Police Commissioner Borse Bhushan Gulabrao and ZP CEO Bhuvanesh Patil were present.

primary_source.content: Bengaluru:&nbsp;This year, the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) honours eight scientists and engineers with its Distinguished Alumnus/Alumna Awards and Young Alumnus/Alumna Medals.The awards recognise alumni/ae who have made exceptional contributions to their professions, to society, and to the Institute. Each nomination is assessed by a committee under the oversight of the Director, IISc.This year's Distinguished Alumnus/Alumna awardees are B S Manjunath, Dipakar Das Sarma, Jagannath Nayak, Maruthi R Akella, and Rajat Moona. The Young Alumnus/Alumna Medals, given to researchers under the age of 40, are conferred on Abhishek Sinha, Geethu Joseph, and Himanshu Joshi.The awardees will be honoured at a ceremony to be held on 19 December 2026, at the JN Tata Auditorium, IISc.Distinguished Alumnus/Alumna Awardees1. B S Manjunath is a globally recognised computer scientist and academic leader, and the Frank Koenig Distinguished Chair in Signals and Systems and Distinguished Professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara, USA. His work spans computer vision, content-based image retrieval, and biological image informatics, including BisQue, an open-source platform for scientific image management adopted as a core service of NSF CyVerse. He contributed foundational video descriptors to the MPEG-7 standard, co-founded the company Mayachitra, and has supervised 53 PhD graduates.B S Manjunath i 2. Dipankar Das Sarma is an internationally renowned condensed matter physicist and materials chemist, currently the ANRF National Science Chair and Emeritus Professor at the Solid State and Structural Chemistry Unit, IISc. His work includes the discovery of the covalent-insulator state, kinetic energy-driven ferromagnetism in Sr2FeMoO6, and depth-sensitive photoemission techniques for probing nanocrystals and buried interfaces. He also spearheaded India's access to international synchrotron facilities, establishing Indo-Italian beamlines at Elettra.&nbsp;Dipankar Das SarmaCentralised street light monitoring system promises better public lighting in Bengaluru 3. Jagannath Nayak is a distinguished defence scientist and Director General of Missiles and Strategic Systems at DRDO. His career spans photonics, fibre lasers, and inertial navigation. He led the indigenous development of high-accuracy Fibre Optic Gyroscopes for programmes such as Akash, Nag, and Astra, and the creation of India's first operational Laser Directed Energy Weapon system. His work has led to complete indigenisation of critical avionics and laser systems.&nbsp;Jagannath Nayak 3. Maruthi R Akella is a globally renowned aerospace scientist and control systems engineer, who currently holds the Cockrell Family Chair in Engineering at The University of Texas at Austin, USA. His research covers spacecraft attitude estimation, adaptive control, vision-guided robotics, and orbital mechanics. His algorithms provided onboard guidance for Intuitive Machines' IM-1 lunar lander mission, the first US moon landing in over 50 years.&nbsp;Maruthi R Akella 4. Rajat Moona is an internationally renowned computer scientist and technologist, and Director of IIT Gandhinagar. His work has shaped India's digital infrastructure, from the Smart Card OS Template Architecture (SCOSTA) behind driving licences and e-passports to India's Electronic Toll Collection system and FASTag. He architected the M3 Electronic Voting Machine, VVPAT, and the National Voters' Service Portal, and as Director General of C-DAC, advanced national supercomputing through PARAM Yuva II.&nbsp;Rajat Moona Young Alumnus/Alumna Medallists1. Abhishek Sinha is a leading theoretical computer scientist, currently a Reader at the School of Technology and Computer Science, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Mumbai. He has resolved long-standing open problems in online learning and network optimisation, including a framework that achieves optimal learning and long-term constraint satisfaction simultaneously. His work has appeared in venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, and IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking.&nbsp;Abhishek Sinha 2. Geethu Joseph is a tenured Assistant Professor at Delft University of Technology, Netherlands. Her work introduces frameworks for resource-aware control systems and sensing methods for autonomous driving, radar, and wireless communications, with industrial partners including NXP, ASML, imec, and TNO. She is an Associate Editor of the IEEE Sensors Journal.&nbsp;Geethu Joseph 3. Himanshu Joshi a researcher in computational biophysics, multiscale molecular simulations, DNA nanotechnology, and an Assistant Professor of Biotechnology at IIT Hyderabad. His work spans aquaporins, ion channels, nanopore sequencing, and water desalination, including artificial water channels for ultrafast water transport and DNA origami-based ion channels.Himanshu Joshi

stories.primary_headline: Steps being taken to curb man-animal conflict in Bandipur: Minister Ramalinga Reddy

primary_source.headline: Steps being taken to curb man-animal conflict in Bandipur: Minister Ramalinga Reddy
primary_source.content: Gundlupet: Minister of Forest, Ecology and Environment Ramalinga Reddy assured that necessary measures are being taken to prevent man-animal conflict in Bandipur forest area.Speaking to media persons, here on Friday, he said, "There is no delay in the probe related to the shootout incident by the Forest department in Hanur, which claimed three lives. The CoD is investigating and we will not intervene. The anti-poaching camps and quarters that were destroyed by mob after the incident are being repaired. The department personnel need not fear and should perform their duties. Besides, there is no permission to possess rifles without licenses. Those possessing the same should surrender to the government, or face legal action."Necessary steps would be taken for the establishing Kaniyanapura elephant corridor of Bandipur Tiger Reserve. Private land if any, would be acquired for the project, he said.Tribal woman killed in tiger attack near Bandipur Reserve in MysuruDiscussions have been held with the State Wildlife Board on announcing M M Hills as Tiger reserve, but locals are against it. The government will take a final decision soon, he said. On illegal resorts and homestays at eco-sensitive zones at Bandipur, he said, permission is given only to resorts that have licenses. Notices are served to those operating without licenses. Some have stay orders from the court. The supervisory committee will monitor this. Reddy held a meeting with the Forest Department officials on the human-animal conflict in the region and gathered information.Principal Chief Conservator of Forest (PCCF) Kumar Pushkar said, "34 people have died due to wild animal attacks in Chamarajanagar district in the last 11 months, and tops the district. Kodagu is in second place. Thirty one tigers have been safely rescued in the last one year."The railway barricades have been useful and the government should grant funds for erecting barricades for 73-kms, he appealed to the minister.Bandipur Conservator of Forest Nandish said, "There are 13 ranges in Bandipur, covering around 1,036 kms. In all, 136 villages come under the forest area. Totally 314 personnel are on duty, with 213 watchers on outsourced basis."Artificial Intelligence cameras and drones are being used to monitor the movement of the wild animals. With this, we get information on the movement of elephants and wild animals near the villages and help to alert the villagers, he said.Reddy said that out of 13 ranges in Bandipur, only four ranges have no man-animal conflict. "Around 38% of the forest is covered with lantana. The biodiversity will be affected if machines are used for clearing it and the forest will be affected if left unattended. Hence, measures would be taken to clear them without affecting the forest," he said.MLA M Ganesh Prasad, APCCF Manoj Ranjan, CCF Malathi Priaya, Ravishankar CF, Mysuru Circle, ACF Paramesh, Vinod were present.

stories.primary_headline: Technology must be guided by character, commitment and compassion: PGIMER Director

primary_source.headline: Technology must be guided by character, commitment and compassion: PGIMER Director
primary_source.content: Mangaluru:&nbsp;Technology and digital advancements must be guided by character, commitment and compassion to ensure their meaningful use for the welfare of society, said Prof Vivek Lal, Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh.Addressing 16th convocation of Nitte Deemed to be University at Deraakatte, he urged students to draw inspiration from Swami Vivekananda's ideals and uphold the values of character, commitment and compassion, which he described as the three essential pillars for the younger generation."Technology and digital assets have no meaning if there is no island of commitment, compassion and character to harness them," he said, emphasising that India had immense technological capabilities as well as the trust and faith of its patients.Mangaluru woman attacked with iron rod in car; man arrested for attempted murder Highlighting the importance of patient-centred healthcare, he said the biggest asset of the country was not technology but the faith patients placed in healthcare professionals. He urged medical graduates to remain grateful to patients and dedicate their knowledge and skills to reduce human suffering.Referring to Swami Vivekananda's historic address at the Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893, Prof Lal said the spiritual leader's teachings on character and social responsibility remained relevant even today. He called upon graduates to give back to society in whatever way possible and make service an integral part of their professional lives.He also cautioned students against becoming overconfident about their digital knowledge in the age of artificial intelligence. While acknowledging AI as an extraordinary technological advancement, he stressed the need to ensure that technology was used responsibly and did not become a threat to humanity.Drawing a parallel with the destructive consequences of nuclear technology, he said humanity must ensure that artificial intelligence was not misused. He urged students to follow the ideals of Swami Vivekananda rather than blindly placing their faith in technology.Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, he said the country could achieve the goal even earlier if the younger generation developed an enlightened mindset and worked with a sense of responsibility.Referring to India's rich medical heritage, he recalled the contributions of Sushruta, regarded as the father of surgery, and Charaka, regarded as the father of medicine. He said their prime focus was healing and relieving the suffering of patients.Nitte DU Chancellor N Vishal Hegde presided over the gathering. Degrees were conferred on 1455 graduates.&nbsp;

stories.primary_headline: Officials inspects cloud kitchens, hotels and sweet manufacturing units in Dakshina Kannada

primary_source.headline: Officials inspects cloud kitchens, hotels and sweet manufacturing units in Dakshina Kannada
primary_source.content: Mangaluru: Following instructions from Health and Family Welfare Minister U T Khader, a team led by Dakshina Kannada District Food Safety Designated Officer Dr Praveen Kumar CH, conducted inspections at the franchise units of shops that supply and sell cakes and ice creams sourced from cloud kitchens and central cake manufacturing units.The inspections were carried out in Surathkal jurisdiction. Officials collected cake samples for laboratory analysis to test whether colours are being used. Maharashtra FDA suspends 19 food licences; acts against Patanjali distributor over 'adulteration'Officials issued warnings against using harmful artificial colours to make cakes visually attractive. Manufacturers were asked to maintain quality and hygiene standards, without the addition of artificial colours while preparing sweets.During the drive, surprise raids were also conducted on local hotels to check kitchen cleanliness. Samples of raw materials and ingredients used in food preparation were sent to the laboratory for testing, and notices were served to establishments failing to maintain  hygiene.

stories.primary_headline: If Dune is this generation’s Star Wars, we are all in big trouble

primary_source.headline: If Dune is this generation’s Star Wars, we are all in big trouble
primary_source.content: According to Florence Pugh, Denis Villeneuve’s stunningly strange and breathtaking universe is the equivalent to George Lucas’ heroic space opera. Let’s hope notA long time ago, far far away, in a galaxy called the 1970s, kids dreamed of joining the rebellion, rescuing a princess and blowing up the Death Star. Peer into the cosmic tea leaves and it would become immediately clear that no amount of evildoing could withstand a neurotic gold butler, a dustbin with ideas above its station and a walking seven-foot tall shagpile carpet with a very low tolerance for disagreement.It is worth remembering this when considering Florence Pugh’s recent declaration, ahead of next month’s Dune: Part Three, that Dune is her generation’s Star Wars. And then wondering how much trouble we might be in if she’s actually right. “I think they brought back movie-going. What an event the second [Dune] was,” Pugh cheerfully told the New York Times. “It was just so lovely to be a part of something that we know is our generational kind of Star Wars.” Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has revived the midnight game launch – but was it worth the wait?

primary_source.headline: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has revived the midnight game launch – but was it worth the wait?
primary_source.content: When our writer found himself among the hundreds on Oxford Street hoping to get their hands on early copies and collectibles, it was a heartwarming reminder of the shared experience of fandom• The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review – a dream come trueIt is Thursday night and I am sat blurry-eyed and runny nosed outside the Argos on Oxford Street. Incredibly, I am far from alone. This is not some strange protest against the popular retailer. When the clock strikes midnight, the lavish 4K Switch 2 remake of beloved N64 classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will be released, and I have joined a lengthy queue of about 500 fans desperate to snag early copies. There are similar events taking place across the world, from Melbourne to Mexico City; at key locations, Nintendo has senior executives waiting at the tills.These days, of course, most video games are bought as digital copies that download straight to your PC or console on the day of release. You don’t even have to get out of bed to start playing. But in a bygone era, when we used to go to shops to buy games, midnight launches offered a space for likeminded enthusiasts to gather and celebrate their fandom. Every Call of Duty, Halo or Grand Theft Auto release would have fans queueing outside branches of Game or Electronics Boutique, many dressed as favourite characters. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: True North by Paul Theroux review – an American’s view of Canada

primary_source.headline: True North by Paul Theroux review – an American’s view of Canada
primary_source.content: The veteran travel writer turns his eye for detail on his northern neighbour and its peoplePaul Theroux’s arrival in Canada doesn’t go well. An immigration officer called Sweeney finds a small pocketknife in his car and fines him $500 for failing to declare a weapon. “I’m going to make you famous,” he angrily tells her, stumping up. Maybe he will, with this book. Canadians are reputed to be polite and easygoing, “slaves to their courtesy”, but the country has changed enormously in recent years. Will Theroux find it stuffed with Sweeney-ites? Luckily the answer is no.He issues a warning that, after 11 previous travel books, this may be his last; global overtourism appals him and so does much travel writing. But he shares Jack Kerouac’s delight in being on the road, and from his home in Massachusetts it’s just a four-hour drive to the border. His purpose is less to check out “the strangers next door” than to visit the village of Yamaska, in Quebec. It was there that a Frenchman called Antoine Theroux settled in the 17th century; a dozen or more Theroux families still live there; one local street is called Rue Theroux. The author isn’t only made welcome but presented with a certificate of honour by the local mayor. He repays the honour with a long chapter of family history. Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: Palo Alto Networks in talks to buy AI agent security startup Clutch for $500M
primary_source.content: Three-year-old Clutch was last valued at $85 million when it raised a $20 million Series A round in January 2025, led by Lightspeed and SignalFire, according to our source. The startup is currently approaching $10 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR). That means the acquisition, if completed, would value Clutch at about 50 times its ARR, a standard way of pricing software companies. Palo Alto Networks and Clutch Security did not respond to a request for comment. The Information was the first to report the acquisition discussions. If the deal happens, it would be Palo Alto Networks’ seventh acquisition this year, according to PitchBook. The cybersecurity giant has a history of buying innovation rather than building it in-house, and it has ramped up dealmaking this year in response to rising AI-driven cyberattacks. Marina Temkin is a venture capital and startups reporter at TechCrunch. Prior to joining TechCrunch, she wrote about VC for PitchBook and Venture Capital Journal. Earlier in her career, Marina was a financial analyst and earned a CFA charterholder designation.

primary_source.content: After some so-so albums, can U2’s new one, Carnaval de Luz, restore them to glory? They discuss male egos, working with Dolly Parton, and explain why, despite Trump, they still believe in democracy – at least in their bandLa Petite Maison, in Nice, has a certain reputation as a five-star celebrity haunt. Beyoncé eats here. So do Elton John, Tom Cruise, Harry Styles and Leonardo DiCaprio, their meals presided over by the restaurant’s founder, Nicole, variously described in print as “eccentric”, “unique” and “truculent” (she’s standing by the entrance when I arrive, and suffice to say, doesn’t look like someone you’d much enjoy being on the wrong side of).It’s enough of a celebrity haunt that the arrival of U2 – still incontrovertibly one of the biggest bands in the world 40 years after they could first reasonably have called themselves such – causes barely a murmur of interest among their fellow lunchtime diners. Then again, Bono is a regular. He was eating on the outdoor terrace the night of Nice’s terrorist attack, on Bastille Day in 2016, in which 86 people were killed. “I climbed through that window and hid under there,” he nods, pointing to a table at the rear of the restaurant. “Nicole,” he adds, “didn’t hide.” Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: What happens after the ‘blue wave’? Our team answers your midterm election results question

primary_source.headline: What happens after the ‘blue wave’? Our team answers your midterm election results question
primary_source.content: Democrats have taken control of Congress in a sweeping blue wave. Our reporters answer your questions about the results of the midterm electionsLive results from the US midterm electionsBgdxc1 asks in the comments: How will this election impact the implementation of NPVIC? How plausible is it that the bills would impact 2028?Sam Levine, voting rights reporter: The mid-term results give the The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact (NPVIC) a serious chance of going into effect. For anyone unfamiliar, the (NPVIC) is an agreement among states in which they agree to award their electoral college votes to the winner of the national popular vote. It would only go into effect if states with at least 270 electoral college votes - enough to win the presidency) agree. Currently, states with 222 electoral votes have agreed to the pact. Democrats won trifectas on Tuesday in states that have 61 electoral votes. Enough states would have to agree to the compact by July 20, 2028 in order for it to go into effect for the next presidential election. Even though Democrats now have enough legislatures to enact the pact, it doesn’t mean it will necessarily go into effect. For one, the states where Democrats have new majorities are the presidential battlegrounds Arizona, Wisconsin, Nevada, Pennsylvania, and Michigan. Those states may not be interested in giving up the attention and focus they get in presidential election years and the federal resources that come with it. There are likely to be a slew of legal challenges to the agreement should enough states join and I would expect the US supreme court to have final say on whether such an agreement is constitutional.Lex McMenamin, movement building reporter: For context, I’ve been closely covering the youth vote since 2018, and it was my main beat up until this January. I’ve been back on it this week, and what an exciting one to return! I feel safe saying it as of right now: Based on exit polling, young people were absolutely a decisive voting bloc this cycle — as they have been in the last two midterm cycles. According to Tufts University’s Center for Information & Research on Civic Learning and Engagement (CIRCLE), which monitors youth civic engagement, 2026 youth turnout was the second-highest midterms turnout in 30 years, second only to the 2018 midterms that brought us the Squad during Trump’s first term. Every youth population that went for Trump in 2024, including both Latino and white men, flipped Democratic by several points. They voted blue on average by +30 in battleground states like Florida and Michigan. These numbers may shift slightly by the spring, when CIRCLE will release full voter data — which, as my colleague Will Craft notes below, are not yet available — but are nonetheless historically notable. Young people are a part of a backlash we’re seeing across generations against Republicans, but it’s absolutely about the issues, too: It was over the economy, corruption, U.S. war-making, and civil rights. They also won a number of seats in state legislatures, continuing to build a presence in government. I’ll dig into the details, and talk to some of those youth voters, in a story coming this weekend. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: The Guardian view on the AI backlash: American voters want a say in their future | Editorial

primary_source.headline: The Guardian view on the AI backlash: American voters want a say in their future | Editorial
primary_source.content: The tech sell-off exposes fragile promises, while Democratic victories offer a chance to protect workers and hold firms accountableThis week’s midterms showed that the political bill for the AI boom is falling due. The Democratic sweep intensified fears over runaway spending, mounting debt and resistance to datacentres, sending tech shares tumbling. On Thursday Wall Street suffered its worst day since the pandemic as $3.2tn was wiped from markets. Anthropic, developer of the Claude chatbot, is hoping to float within the next fortnight for $1.5tn (£1.1tn), but it may not now get even a trillion dollars. The dominant AI chipmaker Nvidia saw its value crash by more than $400bn. The world’s richest man, Elon Musk, lost $113bn in two days.While a few very rich people may be a little less wealthy, the sell-off may not be a bad thing. It brings a needed dose of reality to an industry whose spending plans and valuations depend on heroic expectations of future profits. That is a view held by many influential figures – from Goldman Sachs’ research boss to Nobel laureate Daron Acemoğlu. AI may transform the economy. That does not guarantee investors will earn back the sums being poured into it.Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? stories.primary_headline: Airtel sees churn in customer base due to tariff change, plans more capex on data centre

primary_source.headline: Airtel sees churn in customer base due to tariff change, plans more capex on data centre
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Bharti Airtel has seen a "churn" in its customer base on a quarter-on-quarter basis, following its recent move to shift towards premium mobile plans, a senior company official said on Friday.Airtel has restored the Rs 299 entry-level plan with reduced data benefits after an increase in subscriber churn from its network.The app and website of Airtel have started displaying an option for the Rs 299 plan recharge that will remain valid for 28 days and offer 1 GB data per day instead of the 1.5 GB earlier."The churn that we are seeing in Q2 (second quarter) is for us – largely is combination of two things - the seasonality of Q2 that comes in as well as tariff interventions that we took, where there is always a temporary impact on customer continuity," Bharti Airtel, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Shashwat Sharma said during company's earning call.According to analysts, Bharti Airtel net subscriber addition declined in the September quarter mainly on account of the company's strategy to move towards premium plans."Net subscriber adds, however, declined QoQ from 3.3 million to 0.7 million on account of higher churn (up from 2.6 per cent to 2.9 per cent), likely on account of the plan rationalisation step taken in August 2026, which involved discontinuation of the Rs 299 entry-level prepaid smartphone plan," Citi Research said in a report.Sharma said that usual tariff hikes have worked well for the company's quality customer base."I would say I don't see a constraint in terms of headroom or direct growth, etc that we have, and if ever this happens, we firmly believe we will continue to build industry-leading ARPU in this business," he said.Bharti Airtel's India mobile service revenue in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, has increased by 10.1 per cent year-on-year, driven by customer additions on a year-on-year basis and average Revenue Per User (ARPU) expanding to Rs 271 in Q2 FY27 from Rs 256 in Q2 FY26, the company said.'Applied 5 years ago': Airtel ahead of Musk's Starlink in India's Satellite internet queue, says Sunil Bharti MittalAirtel's India customer base increased by about 11 per cent to 49.86 crore. The company's mobile customer base grew by 3.6 per cent to 37.72 crore, and home service, which includes fixed line broadband services, grew by about 29 per cent to 1.53 crore.Airtel's consolidated capex for the quarter stood at Rs 12,467 crore, including India capex of Rs 9,908 crore during the reported quarter.Bharti Airtel Executive Vice Chairman Gopal Vittal said the company's capital allocation on wireless networks has moderated."If you look at new towers being installed, it's very little now - less than a thousand in the ballpark of 500-600 sites this quarter. Of course, there will continue to be some expansion of 5G. Transport Capex tends to be large because a lot of fiberisation is being done within the company," he said.During the reported quarter, Airtel invested Rs 2,826 crore in a strategic land parcel for data centre expansion in India.Vittal said that the company will continue increasing capex in the data centre business and dividend payout."A lot of the incremental capex would really go behind the growth bets, which is data centres, as we spoke about and cloud. We have already announced a potential continued buyback in Airtel Africa. We've also done that in the Indus (Towers). So, that will continue. You will see that reflected in our conduct; dividend payouts will keep increasing over time," he said.Vital said that the land acquisition for data centres provides the company optionality over time of putting in at least a 400- to 500-megawatt plant."It's a large tract of land, and also it's concentrated in the right locations where the demand seems to be high. We will continue to look at other options for land and build out, as some of that demand from the US may get directed towards India," he said.Vittal said a lumpy capex would be earmarked over the next 12 to 18 months for data centre build-out in Visakhapatnam.

stories.primary_headline: ‘Women’s safety in Hampi at risk as most CCTVs are defunct’

primary_source.headline: ‘Women’s safety in Hampi at risk as most CCTVs are defunct’
primary_source.content: Hosapete: Karnataka State Women’s Commission Chairperson Nagalakshmi Choudhary expressed her disbelief over the fact out of 270 CCTV cameras installed in Hampi, that is flocked by tourists throughout the year, majority of them were not functioning.Speaking to mediapersons here on Friday, Choudhary said that this was found out during her visit to Hampi police station. Tourists throng Hampi throughout the year, and officials’ negligence in repairing these CCTV cameras indicate their concern towards safety of tourist women’s safety in Hampi. She further said that she has directed the officials to set right defunct CCTVs in 15 days.UNESCO delegation to submit report on Hampi in 6 weeks: DCFor the last three days Choudhary has bee visiting various places in the district to receive representations from women. The visit threw up some of the issues including, people staying in Dalmia camp have no road access but have to risk their lives to cross railway lines to reach their homes. She further said that living conditions of gender minorities clearly reflect the officials’ negligence in ensuring them a dignified life. She sought to know why no investigations were launched in cases of ‘baby abandoned’ and also no action was taken against the hospitals. She ridiculed the district administration for not appointing a woman warden for girls hostel.Following complaints that officials failed to address issues concerning women in the district, Choudhary said that ‘Mahila Spandana’ programme must be organised in every district to respond to women’s problems.Before speaking to mediapersons, Choudhary held a review meeting where she directed the officers to respond quickly to women’s problems. She directed officials concerned not to withhold government facilities to former Devadasi women in the name of reviewing the beneficiaries.Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer Garima Panwar, SP S Jahnavi, Assistant Commissioner Kavitha and Women’s Commission secretary Roopa were present.

stories.primary_headline: Exclude vacancies in KK from KPSC purview: Priyank Kharge

primary_source.headline: Exclude vacancies in KK from KPSC purview: Priyank Kharge
primary_source.content: Kalaburagi: District In-charge Minister Priyank Kharge has directed officials to exclude current vacant posts in the Kalyana Karnataka region from the purview of the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) and instead fill them on a priority basis through the Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA).He issued the direction while participating in a meeting of the sub-committee on the development of the Kalyana Karnataka region and the implementation of Article 371(J) of the Constitution held at Vikasa Soudha on Friday.Stating that Article 371(J) of the Constitution was introduced with the objective of ensuring comprehensive development of the Kalyana Karnataka region and providing fair opportunities in education and employment to its people, Kharge said that the officials must treat this significant constitutional mandate with the utmost seriousness. He warned that any form of negligence or delay in the implementation of this provision will not be tolerated.Article 371(J) is a significant constitutional measure, implemented through considerable effort, aimed at the development and protection of the rights of the people of the Kalyana Karnataka region. However, the officials are failing to demonstrate the expected level of seriousness in providing the benefits envisioned by this provision.The people of Kalyana Karnataka rightfully demanding the benefits—such as access to education and employment—to which they are entitled under this provision.Karnataka HC reconstitutes SIT to probe KPSC scam; Hitendra is new chiefThis is a right granted to them by the Constitution itself. Therefore, officials must not treat the implementation of Article 371(J) light, he explained.“The minister said that lack of progress in implementing the clear directives issued during the last meeting indicates that officials have not taken those instructions seriously. Directives issued during meetings should not be confined merely to official records. These must be implemented within a stipulated timeframe, and clear statistics regarding the progress achieved should be presented at the next meeting. The departments must work in co-ordination on matters concerning the development of the Kalyana Karnataka region,” he said.The minister urged officials from the concerned departments to take immediate action to accelerate the process of filling vacant posts in the Kalyana Karnataka region, and to ensure that the constitutional benefits guaranteed to the people of this region under Article 371(J) are effectively delivered.

If the projects are not completed within the deadline, notices will be issued to the contractors and they will be blacklisted,” the minister warned.Residents also brought to his notice the poor condition of the temporary road provided for vehicular movement alongside the construction sites. primary_source.content: Bengaluru: Wipro Limited on Friday announced the appointment of Angan Guha as President and Chief Executive Officer for Americas 2 Strategic Market Unit, effective December 8, 2026. I am confident that his leadership will help us accelerate growth, deepen client relationships, and deliver greater value to our clients," he added.“The evolving AI landscape presents unprecedented opportunities for businesses to innovate and lead. I look forward to collaborating with the talented team at Wipro and helping clients navigate this transformation, drive meaningful business outcomes, and build on Wipro’s strong consulting and technology capabilities,"&nbsp;Angan Guha said.Guha is an experienced technology and business leader who has spent more than three decades driving growth, digital transformation and client success across BFSI, Energy & Utilities and Manufacturing, Wipro said. Prior to serving as Global CEO & Managing Director of Birlasoft Ltd., Guha spent over 28 years at Wipro, holding several senior leadership roles, including CEO of the Americas 2 Business Unit and member of Wipro’s Leadership Team.
