stories.primary_headline: Commercial crop cultivation not a right under FRA; tiger habitat non-negotiable: Supreme Court

primary_source.headline: Commercial crop cultivation not a right under FRA; tiger habitat non-negotiable: Supreme Court
primary_source.content: New Delhi: In a stern message against attempts to legitimise commercial farming inside protected forests, the Supreme Court on Friday held that cultivation of a commercial crop cannot be recognised as a forest right under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, and cannot justify occupation or continued presence in forest areas. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta declared that the sanctity of critical tiger habitat must take absolute precedence. “We must remain conscious of the fact that with Megamalai reserve forest being declared as a Tiger Sanctuary/reserve, the sanctity of the critical tiger habitat has to be given primacy over any claim which intends to encroach upon the forest area,” the court observed.Supreme Court clarifies OBC creamy layer ruling will not reopen past appointments, selections or promotionsThe Tamil Nadu government urged the court to allow silk cotton cultivation in the Megamalai region on historical grounds. To the State’s reliance on historical cultivation of silk cotton, the bench ruled, “cannot, by itself, establish that such cultivation constitutes a forest right” under the FRA. Section 3(1)(c) of the Act recognises only the right to ownership, access, collection, use and disposal of minor forest produce traditionally gathered within or outside village boundaries. Silk cotton is not traditionally collected as minor forest produce, the bench said.The court noted the State's affidavits instead revealed “the promotion and sponsored cultivation of silk cotton as a commercial crop.” “The concept of planned cultivation of commercial crop is totally contrary to the very concept of a naturally occurring minor forest produce,” the court said. “Planned or promoted cultivation of a commercial crop inside the forest areas is completely impermissible as no such right is recognised under FRA, 2006,” it added.Consequently, the bench said the claim that silk cotton cultivation itself justifies the presence of cultivators was “wholly unacceptable.” Tamil Nadu’s Revenue Department had claimed 2,767 persons residing outside forest boundaries were cultivating the crop. The court, however, said outsiders cannot cultivate inside forests without external financing or facilitation. It directed the court-appointed Central Empowered Committee (CEC) to examine this aspect thoroughly for action against violators. The CEC has also been asked to give its opinion on whether silk cotton qualifies as minor forest produce. Building on its May 29, 2026 judgment that ordered structured, time-bound eviction, rehabilitation and ecological restoration in the Agasthyamalai landscape—including division-wise eviction plans, removal of encroachments and a ban on new non-forestry activities—the bench issued further hard directives. Claims of Forest Dwelling Scheduled Tribes or Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must be decided strictly under Section 6 of the FRA and its Rules, not on present occupation alone, it said.Persons in Categories II and III identified by the State are excluded from FRA consideration. The State has been given a final 30-day window to form remaining Gram Sabhas, the bench ordered.The court set up a Special Committee headed by former Chief Justice of India B R Gavai, assisted by a CEC officer and Tamil Nadu’s Principal Chief Conservator of Forests, to scrutinise FRA orders and report to the court in a sealed cover.The matter will be listed on February 1, 2027 for an interim status report. The CEC has also been directed to respond to an NHAI application concerning the NH-744 Puliara–Edamon tunnel proposal.

stories.primary_headline: Deepinder Goyal’s brain chip stirs backlash from medical doctors, they call it ‘clinically bankrupt’

primary_source.headline: Deepinder Goyal’s brain chip stirs backlash from medical doctors, they call it ‘clinically bankrupt’
primary_source.content:
Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal has again found himself at odds with the medical fraternity over his brain monitoring device ‘Temple’ which will be soon available for pre-order in the country in a variety of six shades, Goyal had informed.While his pre-order post has gained a lot of attraction among people, many medical doctors are contesting against it, with the internet famous the LiverDoc calling it ‘fraudulent’.Goyal has allegedly positioned the Rs 85,000 wearable as a ‘fitness’ and ‘well being’ tracker and refrained from calling it a medical product.Designed to rest near the temple, the device has promised to measure entropy, a body metric indicating how hard the body may be working to meet its energy demands.It also alleges to measure ‘cerebral blood flow’ using light-based optical sensors that sit against the skin.&nbsp;Though the company backs the efficacy of the product with an internal experiment on 23 adults and 44 young men, compares its progress to other smart fitness devices that are released before the conclusive results are presented before the public, the medical community stays sceptical of the move, saying its reliability remains unsubstantiated.Dear Concerned Indian Doctors,I see your rage against Temple on X. I have a few points to make:1. First and foremost, a business lesson: if Temple were a scam, and any of what we said weren't true, people would know it in just a few days of using Temple. We have 14-day,…&mdash; Deepinder Goyal (@deepigoyal) November 5, 2026
 

Temple, smart wearable will be up for pre-order this weekend: Deepinder GoyalGoyal versus doctorsIn a heartfelt note on X, Goyal said that he stepped down as CEO of Eternal, parent company of Zomato and since then devotionally worked towards building this fitness product.He said that his company has spent nearly 30 million dollars on its development, out of which 20 million dollars have come from his own pocket.He also informed that the product also carries a 14 days return policy and the customers are willing to give it a try.However, at this juncture, many medical doctors interrupted the flow of his messages and said no amount of emotional struggle, future promises and financial support can substantiate the efficacy of a fitness or health product.They also called out lack of clinical evidence as the biggest drawback with the product.According to some clinicians, including the LiverDoc, the fitness tracker can only measure scalp level blood flow and is not a suitable metric to assess any neurological disturbance.As per reports, light-based sensing systems can only have a superficial depth up to 1 or 2 cm. This may translate only to the outer cortex of the brain.&nbsp;The science used to run this product may not be as effective as a deep tissue ultrasound or a perfusion MRI which can assess blood flow velocity across various regions of the brain.In his defence, Goyal reassured that for now Temple is primarily a fitness product.When DH asked medical doctors on the utility of the fitness tracker, they said it may not have any clinical purpose and the readings obtained might be purely relative.However, some people on X have supported Goyal while saying that no innovation is perfect and lack of absolute evidence must not stop researchers from exploring the potential.To the people disparaging the Indian medical community, please note that we, me included, are not against technological solutions towards improved preventative care. In fact, preventative care is is the heart of medical science.But, let us not confuse fradulently selling… pic.twitter.com/5riczT3cli&mdash; TheLiverDoc™ (@theliverdoc) November 6, 2026
 

Comparing it to other fitness toolsWhen medical professionals questioned Goyal as to why there are no peer reviewed studies on his product, he said that many fitness trackers get released to the public before a comprehensive report of their efficacy is made available to all.“Most wearable companies start with internal studies. Whoop shipped its band in 2015, and the first published validation followed a few years later. We hold ourselves to a higher standard; pre-prints are a step prior to peer reviewed publications, and they are coming up,” said Goyal on X.However, his post attracted a rebuttal where critics like LiverDoc and other clinicians argued that Apple and Fitbit passed multisite clinical trials for FDA clearance.“Other wearables like Whoop (which he cited) measured and validated exactly what the wearable can measure within limits of human anatomy and physiology,” said LiverDoc.Some came in support of Goyal, saying “Indians punish entrepreneurs for taking risks.”However, medical doctors stood their ground by saying they are not against innovation but clinical evidence is the backbone of any fitness or clinical invention.Ending his response on X, Goyal said that some of the features of Temple are not even made public and some of them have nothing to do with doctors.As the line gets blurred between a fitness tracker and medical technology, Temple may have to cover a long path to gain support of healthcare workers.

Syria hosted a series of friendlies at the humble home of Bankstown Bulls, before Lebanon played an all-time World Cup classic against France in a frenzied CommBank Stadium. A few days earlier, Ukraine had played a crucial European Championship match in Belgrade.Lebanon beat France after a wild finish, suggesting they are still among the top eight teams in the world, even if their ranking is far lower due to their inactivity since the last World Cup. The country has been torn apart by the war in the Middle East. “Our last game together was in England in 2022,” said prop Jalal Bazzaz, who played in all three of Lebanon’s matches at the World Cup. “So our aim was just to be good each week. We talked about giving back to where we come from, our roots. It’s in our blood. To put on that jersey, represent my country and put Lebanon on the world stage – it gives people something to smile about, a bit of hope. Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: The Cat in the Hat review – Bill Hader brings plenty but this animated rework is a mess
primary_source.content: The SNL alum has an appealing energy and this is an improvement on the 2003 travesty but it’s also far too long and strangely corporateOver a long enough timeline, perhaps every living alumnus of Saturday Night Live will play the Cat in the Hat. Mike Myers kicked off this unexpected tradition by embodying the furry, anarchic Dr Seuss character for a notoriously, almost defiantly ghastly 2003 live-action treatment. After doing us all the service of killing flesh-and-blood Seuss movies for good, Myers was later followed by a more charming Martin Short (via voiceover on a cute PBS/CBC animated series) and now Bill Hader, stepping into the role for a big-budget animated reboot from the oft-flailing animation division of Warner Bros.Just to be clear, this is the same studio that passed on releasing not one but two well-liked features starring their trademark Looney Tunes characters in the last few years. (Puzzlingly, a new Looney Tunes short starring Daffy Duck nonetheless debuts in front of this movie.) Warner has one of the most storied animation libraries in American cinema (and, for that matter, plenty of great animated TV shows like Batman: The Animated Series and Animaniacs) but as far as features go, they’ve never settled on a clear creative vision. They seem just as adrift in a landscape crowded with serious competitors as they were back when everyone was imitating Disney. Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: Yaxel Lendeborg is the NBA’s most entertaining rookie – and he’s not holding back
primary_source.content: The Warriors’ freshman has spent his first weeks in the NBA antagonizing superstars, speaking his mind and emerging as one of the league’s most compelling personalitiesIf a screen-addled pickup basketball player teleported into the body of a high-level athlete, they might resemble Yaxel Lendeborg. The most commonly cited fact about Lendeborg is that he used to spend 12 to 14 hours a day gaming, and didn’t debut on his high school basketball team until he was an upperclassman. Professional athletes often have origin stories that resemble the superhero more than the mortal, but Lendeborg really was just like us at one point. Lendeborg has also said that prior to entering the NBA, he didn’t really watch it, either. The Puerto Rican forward racked up more than enough accolades in college to qualify for the NBA, including helming Michigan to their first national championship in 37 years, but still. Any of you reading this could smoke the man who may be this season’s rookie of the year in trivia about his profession.The 24-year-old Lendeborg is a forward on the Golden State Warriors, a team caught between the ancient, gleaming remnants of the most fearsome dynasty of the 2010s and its future. The balance didn’t work out last season, as the Warriors produced flashes of old greatness to win one play-in game before flaming out in the next. Such results are a frustrating waste of Stephen Curry’s wonderful form even at 38 years old. Lendeborg is the best hope in a while to help maximize it. But even more importantly, Lendeborg is the character of the season so far. He’s spent its first two weeks antagonizing superstars, firing off unselfconscious takes in the press and vacuuming up the spotlight from his blander peers. What a joy to bear witness to an athlete who probably didn’t even hear the words “media training” until college. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Underdog shows off a 32MB speech model in new demo

primary_source.headline: Underdog shows off a 32MB speech model in new demo
primary_source.content: AI companies across the world are racing to make bigger and better models, but the problem is all of them need massive amounts of processing power. On the other end, some researchers and startups are creating smaller models that can run on edge devices, like your phone or computer. The game features a room with a retro tech theme, a typewriter, and a CRT monitor. There is a desk lamp, which makes a sound when you click its switch. The intro warns users about “intrusive” cloud providers in the town — ostensibly a jab at cloud-based models. You can interact with the typewriter and music tuner. You can type anything on the typewriter using your keyboard, and the game will speak it back. You can also rotate the tuner to generate different kinds of music. All of this works within the browser through Underdog’s speech generation model, which, the company says, can run on most devices without any internet connection. The model has 31 million parameters and is open for everyone to download. While such a small model likely won’t replace bigger models, it may still be enough to drive local assistant experiences or create personalized podcasts.

stories.primary_headline: Physicl raises $10M to make the digital world real enough for robots

primary_source.headline: Physicl raises $10M to make the digital world real enough for robots
primary_source.content: Alex de Vigan’s last business got swamped by the rise of generative AI, but now he’s betting the tech that team had built, a platform for creating tempting product renderings for e-commerce, can be re-purposed to make robots more useful. Founder and CEO de Vigan spent the last decade building nfinite, which made it easy for brands and retailers to create 3D models of their goods and display them online. The arrival of transformer-based AI models led that company to focus more on generative imagery, but de Vigan saw a new purpose for his team and the tech stack they’d built to faithfully render 3D environments. “What we were super unique about doing in 3D, AI was going to replace, but something was missing in AI: its ability to understand, interact, and manipulate space and objects,” de Vigan says. Researchers developing physical AI models to make robots more capable of tasks like handling diverse, small objects have been frustrated by the returns of training them on video, and the expense of gathering data through remote operations. Simulations in digital worlds are seen as a promising solution, but ensuring that these simulated worlds are faithful to real-world physics has proven difficult. De Vigan believes that the pipeline his previous company built to “transform unstructured, incomplete, heterogeneous real-world information into a high-fidelity physical representation… with correct geometry, materials, and physics” can now be used to make physical AI models more effective. Physicl is entering a crowded category of startups vying to provide data and tooling to foundation model builders and robot operators. “The space is very young and very blurry sometimes,” de Vigan admits. There are a variety of companies collecting, labeling, or generating data in different modalities as their customers try to figure out the secret sauce that will make robots live up to their promise.

stories.primary_headline: Rocky review – 50 years on, Stallone’s boxer remains an exhilaratingly gritty contender

primary_source.headline: Rocky review – 50 years on, Stallone’s boxer remains an exhilaratingly gritty contender
primary_source.content: The actor’s triumphant breakthrough has clear ancestors in grimy tales of working-class struggle, but finds a fresh, rousing idealismPeter Farrelly’s new film I Play Rocky is about the underdog-with-heart story of how a great boxing movie got made against the odds with its plucky young untried screenwriter allowed to star. So here is a reissue of that 1976 film for its 50th anniversary. It’s a forthright, rousingly idealistic film, wholesome in its essential patriotism, and which unselfconsciously shrugs off the boxing-movie’s gloomy generic inheritance, throwing away its grim traditional baggage of tragedy, cynicism and loss. It also doubles as a love letter to Philadelphia, the cradle of American democracy.Its writer and insurgent star Sylvester Stallone created the role of Rocky Balboa, a punchy heavyweight fighter just turned 30, making peanuts slugging it out with bums and reduced to collecting debts for the Philly mob; this is an indignity which infuriates his grizzled old trainer and former mentor Mickey (Burgess Meredith) who once saw greatness in Rocky and is disgusted to see him selling out. Rocky is moreover entirely oblivious to national preparations to celebrate the 1976 bicentennial. (Boxing is for this anniversary what country music was in Robert Altman’s Nashville, only without the disorientation and pessimism.) Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Jerusalem artichokes are nutty and delicious, but will run rampant if you let them

primary_source.headline: Jerusalem artichokes are nutty and delicious, but will run rampant if you let them
primary_source.content: Once this tasty tuber is established in your garden, you’ll have a crop for life. Great news – if you can digest themIt’s intriguingly rare to see a crop of jerusalem artichokes, considering how easy they are to grow. They’re part of the sunflower family and, surprisingly, entirely unrelated to the globe artichoke. They produce tall, leggy stems upon which a bright yellow flower blooms, and while they lack the size and sturdiness of sunflowers, they make up for that by appearing in great numbers and developing edible tubers underground. Despite these admirable features, there are good reasons why they are not the most common sight.First, though nutty and delicious, these tubers can be quite hard to digest – earning them the nickname “fartichokes”. They contain a carbohydrate that can be tough on the gut, so it’s recommended that they are cooked well and introduced into your diet incrementally. Having said that, some eat jerusalem artichokes raw, so to those who are devoted to them, or have a fierce digestive system, they’re never off the menu. The second reason they’re not that common, I suspect, is that once you’ve planted them, you’ve probably got them for ever – and, wow, do they know how to run rampant. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Nikita Gill: ‘I read Flowers in the Attic too young. Someone should have stopped me’

primary_source.headline: Nikita Gill: ‘I read Flowers in the Attic too young. Someone should have stopped me’
primary_source.content:
The Indian-Irish poet on the Mahabharata retelling that inspired her to write, Arundhati Roy’s courage, and the poetry of Lucille CliftonMy earliest reading memory
  My father was a sailor and my mother a teacher. They were both voracious readers. I was lucky enough to come from a home full of books and when we joined my father out at sea for extended periods of time, my mother carried plenty of books for me to read. I remember sitting by the porthole in our cabin, looking out at the sea on a sunny day, the ship moving calmly through the waters. I was reading The Tale of Peter Rabbit by Beatrix Potter, a book that still feels like a dream. I was four years old.My favourite book growing up
  There were so many, but when I was a child experiencing the death of my great-grandmother, a maternal figure who I adored, The Neverending Story by Michael Ende became the most essential read for me. I must have read that book a hundred times. I also loved the Winnie-the-Pooh books, Enid Blyton’s Faraway Tree series, the Panchatantra tales, Malgudi Days by RK Narayan and the Asterix comics by René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Enrico Rava Fearless Five with Joe Lovano: Corners review | John Fordham's jazz album of the month

primary_source.headline: Enrico Rava Fearless Five with Joe Lovano: Corners review | John Fordham's jazz album of the month
primary_source.content: (ECM)The Italian trumpeter’s group – featuring an old friend – rip through originals and free improvisation while balancing late-Miles funk with excellent vocals and horn balladsMiles Davis was the gamechanger behind at least three landmark transformations in jazz-making methods between the late 1940s and the 1960s – yet he was perhaps too instinctively lyrical, and too worldly, to take the freedoms he helped unleash too far from the marketplace. In 1960s Europe, a different story emerged, as African American free jazz innovations by Ornette Coleman, John Coltrane, Albert Ayler and others flowed into cultural traditions from Scandinavia to Spain, Soviet Russia and East Germany, inviting unions with contemporary classical and local folk music along the way.But Miles’s unique sound remained as a key inspiration to two gifted trumpeters in Poland’s Tomasz Stańko (1942-2018) and the Italian Enrico Rava, even as they also drew on European eclecticism. Rava continues to rip through the walls of linear post-bop mazes, and use raw sound as if it were his everyday speech, just as Miles once did – as confirmed by Corners, recorded with his young Fearless Five group plus his longtime friend Joe Lovano on saxophones. Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: At least 10 local governments have moved to drop Flock’s surveillance cameras since summer
primary_source.content: The concerns range from privacy to how data is shared (and with whom) to procurement concerns. “We have the tools, training, and experience to locate and apprehend criminals without relying on Flock cameras,” he said in the press release. Tatiana Rice, a senior director for U.S. legislation at The Future of Privacy Forum, told TechCrunch that the backlash to Flock isn’t surprising and only further represents the “growing public skepticism toward technology.” Flock is a target because people can see the sensors and cameras as they drive along roads; data centers have also become physical embodiments of the resentment growing against emerging technology. “A camera at the end of your street is tangible in a way that everyday sharing and selling of personal data online is not,” Rice said. In the resolution, the city said there were “proven instances of Flock Safety infrastructure being used by federal agents for information purposes even without specific authorizations from the contracting locality,” and that the city had reviewed reports that “either intentionally or through its negligence,” Flock had allowed U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) to “use query results from its database of state and local ALPR [automatic license plate reader] data to investigate and persecute immigrants throughout the United States.” “Every day, police departments across the country are using Flock technology to solve serious crimes, locate suspects, find missing people, and make a measurable impact on public safety,” Flock told TechCrunch in a statement. “While we respect every community’s decision, removing a tool that is actively helping solve violent crimes and protect communities moves public safety backward. Every Flock customer owns its data and controls who it is shared with and how it can be used. Flock does not sell data and does not have a contract with ICE.” “Grassroots activists across the country have been demanding that city councils exercise their procurement power to refuse to pay for ALPRs,” Schwartz said, referring to councils’ power to decide what the city buys. He added that activists have been fighting for years and that “many city councils are listening.”

stories.primary_headline: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices

primary_source.headline: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
primary_source.content:
Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password.
The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations.
One connection, works every time, needs no retries
There are two other conditions necessary for successful exploitation. First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions. Second, the target system account must be configured to be passwordless, by way of specifying a "*" in the password field in /etc/shadow, the Linux file where password hashes are stored. Passwordless accounts are commonly used for accounts that use certificate-based authentication. This setting is common for certain types of accounts.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: NASA unveils mysterious X-70 experimental aircraft using AI-generated image

primary_source.headline: NASA unveils mysterious X-70 experimental aircraft using AI-generated image
primary_source.content:
NASA has announced a new experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, that will supposedly feature reconfigurable flight-control technology and a modular design for swapping in different payloads. But much remains unknown about the aircraft’s design and development timeline, even as NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said the X-plane could take flight within two years.
The mystery surrounding NASA’s newest X-plane was exemplified by the agency’s press release, including an apparently AI-generated image of the X-70, showing a dark silhouette vaguely resembling a military fighter jet obscured by smoke. The news was announced by Isaacman during the UP.Summit held at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on November 4.
“The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” Isaacman said. “Its modular design and ability to rapidly swap internal and external payloads will keep our teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next.”Read full article

stories.primary_headline: Google: Schools can keep search while skipping Gemini, but AI search is non-negotiable

primary_source.headline: Google: Schools can keep search while skipping Gemini, but AI search is non-negotiable
primary_source.content:
Google faced the ire of educators and parents earlier this week when it announced a new AI policy for K–12 schools. Google said that it developed its new approach to give schools more control, but early reporting also suggested Google would block search access for schools that didn't want to use AI. Google didn't see the backlash coming, but now that it's here, the search giant is clarifying what exactly its new policy means and what's changing.
The gist of the new policy, according to Google's blog post, is that schools using Google apps will have to opt into its AI products going forward. Since the company considers search part of its AI portfolio (Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search), schools have to specifically turn that on for logged-in student accounts.
When Google revealed its new policy, the company's VP for education spoke exclusively to The New York Times, which interpreted the situation as Google will "turn off search" if schools reject AI. This has a nefarious vibe, but it's probably not the most accurate way to describe how Google's educational AI system will operate. Google's approach may not be entirely altruistic, but it technically offers schools more choice and control than they have now. stories.primary_headline: Software squeezes more data out of Webb Telescope for imaging exoplanets

primary_source.headline: Software squeezes more data out of Webb Telescope for imaging exoplanets
primary_source.content:
With a huge and still-growing catalog of exoplanets, researchers are eager to take the next steps: trying to infer what conditions are like on them, either by imaging them directly or by capturing the light that has passed through their atmosphere. Both are substantial challenges, given the presence of stars that are far, far brighter than light that has come to us via the planet.
While telescopes can be fitted with devices called coronagraphs that block out much of a star's light, there are limits to their effectiveness, caused by noise from subtle variations in the telescope's configuration and pointing between observations. Now, researchers have developed a new software package that optimizes a physical model of the telescope in a way that allows us to better model these differences, producing low-noise imaging of exoplanets.
Point spreads
Central to this work is the concept of a point spread function. If you use a telescope to image a single point of light, it will not appear that way in the actual image. Instead, it will be slightly blurry and spread out, due to imperfections in the telescope hardware and the limits of our ability to keep it pointed accurately through the time it takes to image something. The mathematical description of how a telescope distorts a point of light is called its point spread function.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: Retail vehicle sales in India drop 23.8% in October amid festive calendar shift: FADA

primary_source.headline: Retail vehicle sales in India drop 23.8% in October amid festive calendar shift: FADA
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Retail sales of vehicles in India declined by 23.8% YoY in October, dragged by a sharp decline in the two-wheeler segment amid festive calendar shift, as per data released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA) on Friday.Two-wheeler retail sales dipped by 28.35% to 23.21 lakh units, while passenger vehicle sales fell by 14.23% to 5.07 lakh units during the month.The industry lobby cited the shift in festive calendar and high base of October 2025 as the key reasons for a sharp YoY decline."Last October was an exceptional month that carried both Navratri and Diwali together, over and above the pent-up demand released after the GST 2.0 rate cuts of 22nd September 2025; this year Navratri fell in October, while Dhanteras and Diwali moved into November," said FADA President Sai Giridhar.The October 2026 overall vehicle sales number was 25% higher than the previous month. All segments witnessed a healthy growth on a MoM basis.FADA noted that the YoY fall in sales during October was “base-driven, not demand-driven.”Passenger vehicles sales stood at 5,07 lakh units in October, which was 18.86% higher than the previous month. However, on a YoY basis, it was 14.23% lower.Utility vehicles and a strong launch pipeline continued to anchor demand, while entry-level cars remained the softer spot.Automobile retail sales up 7.71% at 2,81,61,228 units on 2025: FADA"Our pressing concern is inventory: against record wholesale dispatches from manufacturers, passenger vehicle channel stock held at around 43-45 days — unchanged from September. With the Dhanteras-to-Diwali retail wave now under way, we expect inventory to fall back in the 30 days range by the end of the calendar year," said Giridhar.Dhanteras and Diwali are expected to boost November sales.“We are expecting to deliver around 30,000 vehicles on Dhanteras this year,” said Partho Banerjee, Sr Executive Officer, Marketing & Sales, Maruti Suzuki India Limited.“What is particularly encouraging is that the strong momentum is not limited to one day. From Ganesh Chaturthi on September 14 to November 6, we have already recorded retail sales of over 4 lakh vehicles, compared to 3.46 lakh units during the same period last year,” Banerjee added.Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd’s Chief Commercial Officer Amit Kamat said the company is expected to deliver around 12,000 vehicles on Dhanteras.“Since Ganesh Chaturthi, we have recorded retail growth of over 20%, compared with the same period last year, reflecting the strength of underlying demand,” Kamat said.“Dhanteras saw an outstanding response, with single-day deliveries expected to cross 12,000 vehicles. Diwali muhurat deliveries will continue till Wednesday, and we expect this momentum to carry into the coming days,” he added.“Dhanteras and Diwali are one of the most auspicious days to bring home a new vehicle and we are witnessing strong customer demand this year as well. We expect to deliver around 16,000 units, nearly 14% higher than last year,” said Tarun Garg, MD & CEO, Hyundai Motor India Limited.

The couple have a six-year-old daughter and a two-year-old son.Karnataka HC quashes case against Mandya man over 'Pakistan Zindabad' slogan at BJP rally They were living at Madanayakanahalli in Bengaluru, where Rahul was their neighbour. Sahana developed a relationship with Rahul, which led to frequent arguments between her and her husband. Family elders tried to mediate and resolve the issue several times. However, the differences reportedly persisted.The couple had an argument over the same issue last Monday. Following this, Sahana left home on Tuesday and went to her grandmother's house in Gunnayakanahalli, in Mandya district.Rahul visited the village to meet her on Thursday. They had decided to lodge a police complaint against Veeresh. However, they met with a tragic end before they could do so, according to police.

sources.headline: ISRO chief Narayanan calls on TN CM Vijay about preparations to commence rocket launches

brief_bullets: Chennai: ISRO chief V Narayanan called on Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay at the Secretariat on Friday.

Narayanan spoke to Vijay for about half-an-hour against the background of ISRO's preparations to commence rocket launches from the Kulasekarapatnam spaceport in Tamil Nadu from next year, official sources said.
Kulasekarapattinam is near Tiruchendur in Tuticorin district of southern Tamil Nadu.
Tamil Nadu CM Vijay urges setting up of Supreme Court bench in ChennaiNarayanan presented a miniature model of a satellite launch vehicle to Vijay.
On November 5, 2026, Narayanan said that rocket launches from the Kulasekarapatnam spaceport will commence next year.
Speaking on the sidelines of an event, the ISRO chairman said work at the under-construction facility in Tamil Nadu is progressing successfully.
why_it_matters_bullets: Accelerates competitive technological innovation, driving enterprise integration and regulatory review across the sector.
stories.brief: Chennai: ISRO chief V Narayanan called on Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay at the Secretariat on Friday. Narayanan spoke to Vijay for about half-an-hour against the background of ISRO's preparations to commence rocket launches from the Kulasekarapatnam spaceport in Tamil Nadu from next year, official sources said. Kulasekarapattinam is near Tiruchendur in Tuticorin district of southern Tamil Nadu. Tamil Nadu CM Vijay urges setting up of Supreme Court bench in ChennaiNarayanan presented a miniature model of a satellite launch vehicle to Vijay. On November 5, 2026, Narayanan said that rocket launches from the Kulasekarapatnam spaceport will commence next year. Speaking on the sidelines of an event, the ISRO chairman said work at the under-construction facility in Tamil Nadu is progressing successfully. Accelerates competitive technological innovation, driving enterprise integration and regulatory review across the sector.

The probe has been conducted even at the Union Minister's house. A comprehensive probe will reveal the truth, he said.Commenting on Home Minister Priyank Kharge's 'village idiot' statement, he said, the statement issued in village dialect should not be misconstrued.

stories.primary_headline: Factories commence cane crushing

primary_source.headline: Factories commence cane crushing
primary_source.content:
Belagavi: Sugar factories in Belagavi district are all set to commence the 2026-27 sugarcane crushing season, albeit over a month behind schedule.Of the 29 functional sugar factories in the district, 12 are privately owned and 17 are co-operative units. While the factories rely on mechanised harvesting, they also bring in harvesting gangs from Maharashtra to cut the sugarcane.Over the past week, several factories symbolically lit their furnaces to mark the commencement of the crushing season. However, actual crushing and harvesting activities remained stalled as farmers continued their protests demanding higher prices for sugarcane.Karnataka sugarcane farmers withdraw protest, accept Rs 3,600 per tonne price and profit-sharing deal with factories The protests, spearheaded by the Karnataka Rajya Raita Sangha and Hasiru Sene, had continued for over a month, with farmers demanding prices that adequately cover cultivation costs and provide a reasonable profit, besides a share in the profits from the sale of sugar and its by-products.The deadlock was broken after sugar factories agreed to pay Rs 3,600 per tonne and share profits based on increases in sugar prices, following which farmers decided to withdraw their agitation.During the previous crushing season too, farmers had staged protests at Gurlapur in Mudalgi and succeeded in securing an increase in sugarcane prices.Sugarcane price row: Farmers to stage ‘Jail Bharo’ on November 2This season, their demands included a price of Rs 5,500 per tonne, comprising Rs 4,500 from sugar factories and a government support price of Rs 1,000 per tonne, funded through taxes generated from the sale of sugar and its by-products. They also demanded that the Centre increase the minimum selling price of sugar from the existing Rs 31 per kg to Rs 60 per kg, arguing that this would help address the recurring issue of inadequate sugarcane prices.The agitation prompted Union Food and Consumer Affairs Minister Pralhad Joshi to constitute a committee to examine the farmers’ demands, including an increase in the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane, a revision of the minimum selling price of sugar and other demands raised by the protesters.Farmers had blocked traffic on the busy Pune-Bengaluru National Highway at toll plazas in Kognoli in Nippani taluk, Hattargi in Hukkeri taluk and Hirebagewadi in Belagavi taluk. They had also organised a march to lay siege to Joshi’s residence in Hubballi. The march was called off after Joshi assured them that their demands would be considered by November 26.Chief Minister D K Shivakumar had met the protesting farmers at Channamma Kittur and subsequently held discussions with them at Suvarna Vidhana Soudha and the Circuit House in Belagavi. However, these interventions failed to break the deadlock. November 2, farmers launched a jail-bharo agitation, offering to court arrest in support of their demands.Farmers intensify agitation 
in sugarcane-growing districts of north KarnatakaThe breakthrough came after District In-charge Minister Satish Jarkiholi held discussions with representatives of farmers and sugar factories on November 3 and 4. Following the meetings, the factories agreed to pay Rs 3,600 per tonne and also accepted a profit-sharing formula linked to increases in sugar prices.Karnataka Rajya Raita Sangha and Hasiru Sene state president Chunappa Pujeri said the organisations had decided to withdraw the agitation following the agreement on higher sugarcane prices and profit-sharing.“Farmers could get up to Rs 4,350 per tonne this season, and we are hopeful of securing this amount, given the shortage of sugarcane across the world. Sugar factories will now commence crushing operations, and harvesting will begin,” he said.

stories.primary_headline: Centralised street light monitoring system promises better public lighting in Bengaluru

primary_source.headline: Centralised street light monitoring system promises better public lighting in Bengaluru
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: The Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda, on Friday, inaugurated the city's first Centralised Control and Monitoring System (CCMS) for streetlights. The centre established in Jayanagar is aimed to improve the condition of streetlights and automate the operations significantly.&nbsp;According to the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), across the city, close to five lakh LED streetlights, comprising three lakh newly installed LED lights and 1.97 lakh existing LED lights will be integrated with CCMS and 24677. The initiative will also help bring down expenditure on power since it is expected to provide over 54% energy savings.Dark streets, delayed smart lighting: Bengaluru’s LED upgrade struggles to get on trackThe system, once implemented across the city, will help improve the public lighting infrastructure across the city significantly since it has a capability to flag problems automatically. “The key advantages of this technology is its ability to proactively detect faulty or non-functional streetlights. This will enable maintenance teams to identify and attend to faults without waiting for citizens to report them. The advanced CCMS will enable centralised as well as individual monitoring of streetlights, automated ON/OFF scheduling, GPS-based asset tracking, real-time energy consumption monitoring and automatic identification of non-glowing, flickering and partially glowing streetlights,” a statement by the GBA said.Better streetlights and faster turn around time for repair will also improve public safety, Gowda said. “Beyond energy savings and reduced electricity expenditure, the initiative is expected to improve road illumination, enhance public safety, reduce maintenance response time and minimise energy wastage,” he said.GBA chief inspects Bengaluru West infrastructure projects, directs fast-tracking of worksIn the coming days, GBA plans to have four dedicated Streetlight Central Control Rooms across the city. These control rooms will monitor streetlight performance, electricity consumption and fault alerts through a centralised digital dashboard.The GBA is also planning to set strict timelines for the repair of streetlights identified to be faulty.&nbsp; “Dedicated field maintenance teams will be deployed to address identified faults and citizen complaints, with a provision to resolve streetlight-related issues within 24–48 hours of identification or registration. Failure to resolve faults within prescribed time limits will automatically trigger penalties on maintenance contractors,” the statement by GBA said.Streetlights are one of the highest reported problems in the city apartment from waste management. DH had earlier reported that close to 6,000 complaints were reported regarding faulty streetlights in September and on average close 5,000 complaints are being reported every month.

stories.primary_headline: ‘He left the world in ruins’: the author who defied the Taliban and burning tyres to tell Alexander the Great’s epic story

primary_source.headline: ‘He left the world in ruins’: the author who defied the Taliban and burning tyres to tell Alexander the Great’s epic story
primary_source.content: He is the most powerful ruler ever – and his first biographer was crucified. What drew Edmund Richardson, winner of the £50,000 Baillie Gifford prize, to his short tumultuous life?He was the most powerful man in the world but he was brought down by one battle too many after a decade at the top. The story of Alexander the Great might be more than 2,000 years old, but it seems timely that a new biography of the ancient ruler won the Baillie Gifford prize for nonfiction just as President Trump took a battering in the US midterms. “This is a moment,” says its author Edmund Richardson, “where people are finding that there are limits to what unlimited wealth and power can do, and that humanity catches up with you, whether you like it or not. Alexander wants to transform the world – and he leaves it in ruins.”Wearing a purple velvet jacket, purple scarf and matching socks, with a high forehead and corona of auburn curls, Richardson himself might have stepped out of an earlier age. It is hard to imagine anyone less like history’s favourite mob boss than this softly spoken professor of classics. We are having coffee at the offices of the PR company for the Baillie Gifford prize, the view of the City of London skyline from the floor to ceiling windows a reminder of 21st-century power and economics. stories.primary_headline: Government contingency plan ready for drop in rabi sowing

primary_source.headline: Government contingency plan ready for drop in rabi sowing
primary_source.content: New Delhi: It is too early to raise alarms over a sharp drop in rabi sowing this season, a senior agriculture ministry official said on Friday, stressing that adequate time remains for planting and that the government has prepared a contingency plan for the first time.As of October 30, total rabi acreage stood at 37.56 lakh hectares, down 46 per cent from 69.02 lakh hectares a year earlier, according to official data.Wheat, the main winter crop, covered just 19,000 hectares against 3.34 lakh hectares last year. Pulses fell to 9.45 lakh hectares from 19.56 lakh, oilseeds to 20.97 lakh from 38.62 lakh, and other crops also lagged.“Sowing can be undertaken till December. The current month is crucial,” the official said, attributing the delay largely to a 13 per cent deficient monsoon that left residual soil moisture low in many areas.The ministry has drawn up a dynamic contingency plan covering 225 districts to address moisture stress and weather variability. Farmers in water-scarce regions are being encouraged to grow less water-intensive crops such as chickpea, mustard, lentil and millets. Climate-resilient and heat-tolerant seeds are being promoted.Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has directed officials to accelerate sowing after the kharif harvest and make optimal use of remaining moisture. The government reports adequate stocks of fertilisers and certified seeds, with supply chains coordinated down to the district level.A soil health policy aimed at cutting chemical fertiliser use is expected in the next three to four months. Officials also noted a sharp decline in stubble-burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana, stating it is not a major contributor to Delhi-NCR pollution, while efforts continue to reduce edible oil import dependence.

stories.primary_headline: Telangana woman studying in US goes missing after stepping out for evening walk

primary_source.headline: Telangana woman studying in US goes missing after stepping out for evening walk
primary_source.content: Hyderabad: Talking to their daughter, who studies in the US, every day was a routine for Koya Yadagiri Reddy and Roopa of Shabdulapuram village in Nalgonda district, Telangana. They spoke to her before she left for college and again after she returned from her part-time job. Since November 2, however, there has been no word from Sreeja Koya, 23, who has gone missing in Boston, USA.Sreeja, their only daughter, was last seen after she went out for an evening walk. “On November 2, after she came back from work, her roommates were to celebrate the birthday of one of them. As is her habit, she went out for an evening walk, promising to be back for the celebration. But she did not return, and her roommates tried to reach her. At first, the phone rang, but she did not pick up. After some time, it was switched off. They then contacted us in India to asked if she had called us. We were clueless and worried about what happened to her,” a distressed Yadagiri Reddy said on Friday.Local reports in the US said Sreeja lives in the Dorchester area of Boston and was last seen at around 9.45 pm local time at Edison Green, wearing a black jacket and blue jeans. She is suspected to be near Carson Beach or Harbor Point. Her friends filed a complaint with the Boston Police on November 3, and on November 4, the Boston Police Department issued a missing person alert.Sreeja KoyaPolice are learnt to be focusing on several areas based on the last known location of her mobile phone and are searching in particular around Carson Beach and Harbor Point.According to family members, Sreeja was determined from childhood to pursue higher education in the US. She left for the US last year and is studying at the University of Massachusetts in Boston. Alongside her studies, she works part-time at a recently secured job on the university campus. The family has also appealed to Telugu associations and the Indian diaspora in the US to help trace her.“Koya was last seen leaving her residence in the area of Edison Green in Dorchester at approximately 9:45 PM on Monday, November 2, 2026. Koya is described as an Indian female, 5’3”-5’5” in height, with a thin build and black hair. Koya was last seen wearing a black jacket and blue jeans. She may be in the area of Carson Beach or Harbor Point. The Boston Police Department is actively working to locate Sreeja Koya and urges anyone with information regarding her whereabouts to call 911 or contact District C-11 (Dorchester) Detectives at (617) 343-4335. Community members wishing to provide information anonymously may do so via the CrimeStoppers Tip Line,” said the Boston Police Department in a missing person alert.

primary_source.content: Ahead of the Diwali (Deepavali) festival, Reliance Jio has announced a new industry-first three-year prepaid plan in IndiaIt is offering several lucrative benefits, including unlimited super-fast 5G data with a 2.5 GB cap per day, unlimited voice calling, 100 SMS per day, and a validity of 1095 days. Quick summary - click for full detailsConcise summary of key highlightsReliance Jio launches 3-year 5G unlimited prepaid plan ahead of DiwaliIn one lineReliance Jio launches a new three-year unlimited 5G prepaid plan ahead of Diwali, featuring bundled OTT and AI tool subscriptions.Key highlights• Three-year 5G prepaid planReliance Jio has introduced a long-term plan offering unlimited 5G data capped at 2.5 GB per day, unlimited voice calling, and 100 SMS per day.• Bundled entertainment and AISubscribers receive JioHotstar Mobile + Hollywood access, Canva Pro Lite with 50GB cloud storage, and 50GB of JioAICloud storage.• Anniversary and festive offersThe launch coincides with rollout offers leading up to Jio's 10th anniversary in 2026, including various voice-only and data packs.Key statistics3 yearsPlan validity2.5 GBDaily 5G data cap50GBCanva cloud storage50 GBJioAICloud complimentary storage2026Milestone anniversary yearProcessed with AI. Reviewed by DH Digital Team.In addition to connectivity benefits, subscribers are eligible to claim JioHotstar Mobile + Hollywood access for live sports, premium entertainment, Hotstar Originals and blockbuster Hollywood content.Google Labs' experimental AI app 'Dreambeans' makes its debut in IndiaFurthermore, they also get Canva Pro Lite (12 months). With Canva's AI tools, users can do school projects for kids, office presentations and create fancy festive greeting cards on a phone or on a computer.For beginners, it also offers multiple templates to start off a project and supports Indian languages for more personal birthday greeting cards. Canva Pro Lite also includes 50GB cloud storage, and with Canva Pro, users get 100GB cloud storage.Reliance Jio logo.And the new Jio prepaid plan offers JioAICloud with 50 GB of complimentary cloud storage for secure storage and access to files, photos and documents. The 3-year Unlimited Plan will be available starting November 7 across MyJio, Jio.com, Jio stores, retail outlets, and other Jio recharge channels nationwide.2026 is a milestone year for Reliance Jio, as the company completes its 10th anniversary. To mark the celebrations, it has been rolling out lucrative offers to customers including the Amazon Prime Lite free for one year to select JioHome users, mega anniversary Rs 3,599 plan offering 2.5GB per day (912.5 GB in total), unlimited voice calls, and 100 SMS per day. It also offers a free Google Gemini Pro plan for 18 more months, worth Rs 35,100. For Rs 399 plans, users will be entitled to get 12 months of free access to Canva Pro worth Rs 4,000.For the Rs 349 and all other 2 GB/day prepaid plans, subscribers are entitled to get 12 months of free access to Canva Pro Lite worth Rs 1,590.Most recently, it launched several voice-only plans with validity ranging from 28 days to 336 days.Reliance Jio is offering a Rs 1,748 plan for 336 days (almost 11 months) with unlimited voice calls, 3,600 SMS, in addition to access to JioTV and a JioAI Cloud subscription.Similarly, there is a Rs 448 plan with validity for 84 days (almost three months) with unlimited voice calls, a 1,000 SMS limit and access to JioTV and a JioAI Cloud subscription.Reliance Jio is also offering a Rs 197 plan (full calendar month) with unlimited voice calls and 300 SMS per month. There is also a Rs 196 plan with the same benefits, but valid for 30 days.There is a 28-day validity plan for Rs 177 with unlimited voice calls and 300 SMS benefits. And Rs 147, the most affordable plan, comes with 22 days' validity. It offers unlimited voice calls and 300 SMS benefits.It also offers a Rs 15 unlimited data pack. primary_source.content: New Delhi: With rice prices rising amid a deficient and uneven monsoon, the Centre on Friday directed traders, retailers, wholesalers, processors and millers nationwide to declare their rice and paddy stocks. It also permitted five southern states to impose stock limits to check hoarding.Under a November 6 order, all such entities must declare holdings in six categories—Basmati rice, non-Basmati premium rice, non-Basmati rice, parboiled rice, broken rice and paddy—on the Food Stock Portal every Friday. Unregistered units or those breaching limits face action under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.Separately, the Centre consented to Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana imposing stock limits on paddy and rice until January 31, 2027. Authorities will monitor compliance to ensure availability and prevent black marketing.Karnataka teacher conserves 1,540 traditional rice varieties, earns national recognitionTo boost supplies, additional rice has been allocated to NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar for sale as Bharat Rice, with a focus on southern states. The Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) e-auction target for 2026-27 has been doubled to 50 lakh tonnes from 25 lakh tonnes. About 25 lakh tonnes were sold by October 31, more than double last year’s figure for the same period.Trade experts link the price rise to uneven rainfall, which has driven inflation especially in premium non-Basmati varieties. Retail rice inflation climbed to 8.25% year-on-year in September from 5.89% in August, with average prices around Rs 48.23 per kg—about 12% higher than a year ago.Kharif paddy acreage fell nearly 4% to 42.68 million hectares. Output is estimated at 147 million tonnes against last year’s record 154 million tonnes. While government stocks remain comfortable, pressure is sharper in southern premium grades such as Sona Masoori.

stories.primary_headline: Spice Girls: The Singles Collection review – stop fleecing your fans right now, thank you very much

primary_source.headline: Spice Girls: The Singles Collection review – stop fleecing your fans right now, thank you very much
primary_source.content: (Virgin)The reunion that fans were hoping for turns out to be a cash-grab box set – though there is a worthwhile curio featuring Posh on lead vocalsIs there a more taunted fanbase than that of the Spice Girls? Seemingly every other week a story – usually perpetuated by Mel B, the band’s number one cheerleader – appears in the tabloids hinting at some sort of reunion. Or film. Or documentary. Swift denials then emerge, typically linked to Geri or Victoria, and all is calm until a week or so later.So when teasers showing landmarks from 1996’s Wannabe video suddenly appeared on the band’s official social media accounts in September, it felt as if the fans had something tangible to celebrate. The comments quickly filled with hopes of another reunion tour following 2007’s full-band jaunt and 2019’s Posh-less stadium trek. In a music landscape littered with nostalgia tours, surely Ginger, Scary, Baby, Sporty and (maybe) Posh could strap on some Buffalo boots for a final zig-a-zig-ah? Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: ‘I’m never going to be bloody Robert De Niro!’: Rob Brydon, the most chipper man on TV

primary_source.headline: ‘I’m never going to be bloody Robert De Niro!’: Rob Brydon, the most chipper man on TV
primary_source.content: The nicest man in acting is back with new comedy, Bill’s Included. He talks about rejecting Hollywood, refusing to play a villain – and why he just can’t make fun of Steve Coogan‘I’m a nice person, you know,” says Rob Brydon, as I met him in a basement green room of the BBC, where probably nobody with such a mellow ego has ever sat. “I am a people-pleaser. That’s who I am.” It’s an unnecessary clarification – at 61, he’s been nice on TV, as himself and in character, for most of our adult lives.We’re here to talk about his new six-parter, Bill’s Included, but his character in it, the eponymous Bill, is such a distillation of pure Rob Brydon that it’s (accidentally, he says) a celebration of his entire career. As the show opens, Bill has just been left by his wife, who’s run off with the gardener. At no point does he ever fire the guy – “I like him!” – but otherwise, his life is completely upended. The utterly plausible cocktail of his civic mindedness and howling loneliness drives him to take in four lodgers, local university students. Continue reading...

primary_source.content:
Inspired by everything from Radiohead to Deerhoof and Linda Perhacs, the west country band merge disparate styles into solid anthemsFrom Bristol, UK
 
 Recommended if you like Puscifer, Julie Christmas, the Mars Volta
 
 Up next Supporting Every Hell at Bristol’s Exchange, 4 December; playing UK festivals Strangeforms, Noizzefest and Arctangent in 2027Even a cursory scroll through Sans Froid’s influences will make you expect chaos. In interviews, members of the west country rockers have acknowledged Radiohead, the Mars Volta, the immersive folk of Linda Perhacs and even the haywire opera/metal/breakbeat of French button-pusher Igorrr. Combine that array with the four-piece’s sole collective inspiration – San Franciscan indie experimentalists Deerhoof – and it’s amazing there’s any coherence at all. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: After the midterms, the global right is reeling. But the danger of Trumpism will never be gone | Jonathan Freedland

primary_source.headline: After the midterms, the global right is reeling. But the danger of Trumpism will never be gone | Jonathan Freedland
primary_source.content: Yes, the Republicans suffered humiliating defeat. But the fact that a Trump presidency was even possible means something like it could happen againHe’s down, but not quite out. Barring divine or other intervention, Donald Trump will remain in the Oval Office for a further two years and 10 weeks. Or, as the White House put it in a plaintive social media post brimming with neediness: “PSA [Public Service Announcement]: Trump is still your president.” But that’s not the only reason why the global celebrations that greeted the Democratic tidal wave that swept Republicans out of even their deepest heartlands should be tempered, if only a tad.Don’t get me wrong, the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections are cause for genuine international jubilation. The defeats of Trump allies in Serbia and Brazil were delicious appetisers, but this was the feast. No mere electoral setback in line with midterm tradition, this was a thorough repudiation of the second Trump presidency and of Trumpism. The 16% swing to Democrats in the popular vote for the House of Representatives was greater even than the 11.2% swing recorded in the Watergate midterms of November 1974, following the resignation in disgrace of Richard Nixon. Trump had worked hard for many months to undermine these elections, either by gerrymandering districts in his favour or preparing the ground for a later claim the vote was rigged, but to no avail: the democratic system proved too resilient, and the American public too determined to have their say. And have it they did, in a voice loud and clear. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Hockey’s streaming spree means there’s one fewer thing holding Canada together

primary_source.headline: Hockey’s streaming spree means there’s one fewer thing holding Canada together
primary_source.content: A shared joy of the sport has united Canada for much of its history. But it’s becoming increasingly difficult – and expensive – to watch games on televisionThe Oilers lost to the Detroit Red Wings on 26 October, but Edmonton captain Connor McDavid got an assist anyway. He’s been doing that a lot lately. Just 16 games into the year, McDavid has 31 assists. It’s the fastest anyone has ever hit that milestone in any NHL season. But on that night in late October, many fans in Edmonton were unable to see McDavid’s feats – including patrons of a local bar – because it was one of nine Oilers games this season that are only available via a subscription to a premium streaming service.It’s the same story in every Canadian NHL city, thanks to changes to broadcasts that have meant that a handful of games for each team are now only available with a C$12.99 per month subscription to Sportsnet+, a streaming channel owned by Canadian telecom juggernaut – and owner of the Toronto Maple Leafs – Rogers Communications Inc. But it’s not just Sportsnet+. The NHL also expanded its broadcast deal with Amazon, so when, two nights after the game against Detroit, the Oilers played their provincial rival, the Calgary Flames, only Amazon Prime subscribers could watch (true to form, McDavid got two assists in that one). Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: ‘Mom encouraged me to get breast implants’: Disney child star Christy Carlson Romano on fame, family and freedom

primary_source.headline: ‘Mom encouraged me to get breast implants’: Disney child star Christy Carlson Romano on fame, family and freedom
primary_source.content: She started acting at six and by 16 was starring in Even Stevens with Shia LaBeouf. Then her career fell apart. Here, she explains how she survived growing up in the spotlightIn a class at college, Christy Carlson Romano was encouraged to think about her “community”. Who were their people, the tutor asked the class, and where did they belong? The answer that popped into Carlson Romano’s head was child actors, but not the ones that went on to have successful grown-up careers. “The ones who were once the shining stars,” she writes in her memoir, “and who are now just trying to find out their places in the world.” Carlson Romano had returned to college after initially dropping out. She had survived sexual assault and toxic relationships, was broke and drinking too much. But before all that, she had been a teenage Disney star. She had made it.The title of her memoir, Once Upon a Trainwreck, gives you a flavour of where Carlson Romano, 42, is coming from, but what’s most striking isn’t that she goes off the rails (she doesn’t, hugely, compared to other former child stars), but how sensible and mature she is as a child. It’s alarming. When fans recognise her now – she was in the popular Disney series Even Stevens which started in 2000 – they tell her she was a huge part of their childhoods. She had been acting the part of a normal suburban girl, the perfectionist Ren Stevens, while having no idea what that was like. She was already a mini adult. Continue reading...

Instead, it’s a culture-clash skewering of conservative and liberal values worthy of its Palme d’Or‘Pffff!” Cristian Mungiu lets out an exasperated sigh. We are sitting in the basement of a London hotel, at the end of a long morning of back-to-back interviews for the Romanian film-maker, and his press handler has just snuck into the room to remind him of his next appointment across town. But Mungiu blanks him and leans on to his table, because he wants to tell one more story.In 2013, Mungiu was part of a delegation of European auteurs who travelled to Brussels to meet the then president of the European Commission, José Manuel Barroso. primary_source.headline: ‘Every day, someone loses a hand or a leg’: the brutal reality of India’s textile recycling industry
primary_source.content: In Panipat, 1m tons of used clothing a year are turned into products for global brands, but dangerous machinery and few safeguards mean life-changing injuries are commonFor three months, Suraj Kumar’s job was to feed discarded clothes into shredding machines in Panipat, an industrial city in the north Indian state of Haryana. Clothes discarded in the US, Canada and Europe arrive in the city to be torn back into fibres and spun into yarn, feeding a textile recycling industry that supplies markets across the world.Suraj, 19, had travelled from West Bengal state to work in Panipat’s factories, following his cousins and friends who had already found jobs there. He hoped to earn enough to send money home to his parents. But in late August, an electrical short circuit in the machine propelled him into the shredding mechanism. The accident crushed both arms. stories.primary_headline: Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook review – the heir to a legendary eatery … who sets soup on fire

primary_source.headline: Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook review – the heir to a legendary eatery … who sets soup on fire
primary_source.content: She is completely baffled in the kitchen, but the star valiantly resurrects her family’s famous restaurant. Her journey is chaotic, hilarious – and deeply movingIt starts both very well and very badly does Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook. On the one hand, our host’s absolute ignorance of how food works – or pans, or knives, or plates – has a refreshing authenticity about it. Too often in these shows, in which a celebrity goes on A Journey to acquire basic knowledge in what is generally considered to be a normal field of human endeavour, their lack of exposure to it or inability therein is pretended or hammed up. But actor, rapper and comedian Awkwafina – real name Nora Lum, which is what she uses for this series beyond the title, for reasons that will become clear – is the real, wholly baffled deal.Non-game recognises non-game, and as a kitchenphobe myself, I see the truth in her crouched stance by the oven or hob, fearful yet hostile to anything they may ask of her. We see her pour milk over a couple of eggs she has just lobbed doubtfully into a pan, the tentativeness with which she approaches spatulas and ladles, the hatred in her eyes when presented with raw ingredients – it all speaks to someone who has remained truly untouched by the culinary arts and was, at least until a commissioning editor approached with an idea, happy to remain so. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Serbia has banished the monsters from Belgrade – it was, and still is, a truly wonderful revolution | Barbi Marković

primary_source.headline: Serbia has banished the monsters from Belgrade – it was, and still is, a truly wonderful revolution | Barbi Marković
primary_source.content: The Student List has shown my generation, who protested against the Milošević regime in the 1990s, how we should have done itOn Halloween, a few days after a student-led movement swept aside an illiberal, seemingly invincible regime in my native Serbia, I was sitting on the Vienna tram and watched various friendly and malicious monsters getting on and off around me. Witches, devils and unicorns were politely making their way to their respective parties.Not all monsters wear fancy dress. Later that evening, I walked past a Serbian restaurant; in front of it stood a group of grumpy-looking men. They were smoking, spitting and swearing. I recognised the hardened, couldn’t-care-less attitude, the smell of corruption, the penchant for violence. Yet they looked as though their lives were coming to an end. These men are the losers of the revolution that is taking place in Serbia. Their smuggling routes and deals are under threat. Their criminal networks no longer function. Continue reading...

primary_source.content:
Color us nostalgic.
Sony has brought back the MDR-3-series headphones that debuted in 1979 alongside the Walkman TPS-L2 cassette player.

      In this marketing image Sony shared, you can see the Walkman TPS-L2.
        Credit:
          Sony
      
Originally called the "MDR-3L2," the first Walkman headphones were known for their sleek, adjustable gray plastic headband, which extended via metal sliders and ended in signature orange, circular ear cushions. The lightweight, on-ear headphones are a contrast to the bulky headsets that are popular these days, which use wide, cushioned headbands for long-term comfort and large earcups that can support big drivers and are often heavily padded for noise isolation.Read full article

primary_source.headline: Songs from the Firefront by Tim Winton review – climate urgency verges on panic, with moments of wonder too
primary_source.content: The masterful Australian writer has become a kind of prophet – and his dramatic and moving new essay collection challenges us not to look awayTim Winton has been working his themes for almost 50 years in a palimpsest of 32 books: family, manhood, land and ocean; what it is to be human and Australian; intimate pleasures and anxieties that feed his fiction. The distinctive quality of his new collection of memoir and essays, Songs from the Firefront, is urgency verging on panic. He’s an elder in his 60s, with limited time to get his messages across before we all go up in flames.Living on the western edge of Australia, Winton has been an eloquent climate-change activist for decades. He has fought, with tenuous success, to protect Ningaloo Reef. He entrances us with Scheherazade stories that blend crystalline nature writing and terrifying facts. The loss has accelerated now, he says, and the danger is immediate.Songs from the Firefront by Tim Winton is out now through Hamish Hamilton/Penguin Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: BMW bumps battery for the better: The 2027 i7 60 xDrive, driven

primary_source.headline: BMW bumps battery for the better: The 2027 i7 60 xDrive, driven
primary_source.content:
BMW provided flights from Washington, DC, to Los Angeles and accommodation so Ars could drive the 2027 i7 as well as the 2027 iX5 and X5. Ars does not accept paid editorial content.
When BMW debuted the new 7 Series in 2022, it set a new standard for large luxury sedans, increasingly irrelevant though that class is. Rather than siloing off an electric alternative like Mercedes, with its EQS alongside the normal S-Class, BMW simply made the powertrain an option. Stick with a V8 if you want, or consider the rather good electric version instead—only subtle differences like the badging and lack of exhaust pipes give the game away.
Since then, BMW has brought out a string of even newer electric vehicles for the 5 and 3 Series (plus their SUV counterparts). It has switched from battery packs made of prismatic cells to more energy-dense arrangements of cylindrical cells. The motors are still electrically excited synchronous ones, but now the drive units feature silicon carbide inverters and more compact packaging.
This sixth-generation electric powertrain was designed for the clean-sheet Neue Klasse family, which also threw out the legacy cruft of dozens and dozens of discrete single-function electronic control units for a handful of powerful domain controllers. These computers take over those functions but with much faster processing power—and therefore more capabilities in terms of chassis control or powertrain efficiency—as well as the ability to be more easily updated.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: Kalshi court losses pile up as judges refuse to block state gambling laws

primary_source.headline: Kalshi court losses pile up as judges refuse to block state gambling laws
primary_source.content:
Kalshi is having a bad week in the federal court system. Two circuit appeals courts rejected the prediction market's latest attempts to block state gambling laws in Connecticut, New York, and Nevada. Kalshi is separately facing a new lawsuit filed by the Arkansas attorney general.
In all cases involving Kalshi and state governments around the US, the main issue is whether state gambling laws apply to prediction markets despite Kalshi's claim that its platform offers "swaps" that can only be regulated by the US Commodity Futures Exchange (CFTC). The Trump administration is on Kalshi's side, with Donald Trump Jr. serving as an advisor to Kalshi in exchange for a generous equity deal.
"Kalshi insists that its products are not gambling," but "Arkansas law is concerned with substance, not semantics," Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin said yesterday when announcing his lawsuit against Kalshi. Kalshi's prediction market lets customers "wager money on the outcome of just about anything" despite the fact that "gambling on an unregulated platform is squarely prohibited by Arkansas law," he said.Read full article
